questions.text: It is likely that the nonmedical use of prescription stimulants can improve academic performance in the long run.
Which of the following statements regarding HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) Laws is TRUE?
options: HIPAA was originally proposed to enable people to change their jobs and keep their insurance.
HIPAA regulations regarding how Protected Health Information can be disclosed and utilized apply only to minors.
If a breach of a patient’s Protected Health Information occurs, the provider to must disclose the breach only if the provider determines that the breach is serious enough to warrant reporting.
The TPO exception to HIPAA allows disclosure of information via Telecommunication devices, Phone, and Other digital media.
Healthcare professionals can communicate with any member of a patient’s immediate family about their treatment without any permissions from the patient.

questions.text: In the small group sessions we discussed a case in which a dentist was concerned that his patient who needed antibiotic prophylaxis would go to a different dentist and not receive the necessary antibiotic prior to dental treatment. The patient would not allow this dentist to inform the new dentist of the patient’s condition. Consider the following statements: I. The ethical principles of BENEFICENCE and NON-MALEFICENCE support the argument that the original dentist should not inform the new dentist of the need for antibiotic prophylaxis. II. The ethical principle of AUTONOMY supports the argument that the original dentist should inform the new dentist of the need for antibiotic prophylaxis.
options: I is TRUE and II is FALSE.
I is FALSE and II is TRUE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the practice of the professions of dentistry, dental hygiene, and registered dental assisting, in NYS is FALSE?
options: Rules and regulations including those pertaining to licensing of dentists are determined by the NYS Education Department Office of the Professions.

To qualify for a license as a dentist in NY State, an applicant must satisfactorily complete a clinicallybased postdoctoral general practice or specialty dental residency program, of at least one year's duration, in a hospital or dental facility accredited for teaching purposes by an approved national accrediting body.
To qualify for a license as a dentist in NY State, an applicant must be of good moral character.
When renewing one’s NY State registration to practice, a dentist must satisfy mandatory continuing education requirements.

Procedures that may legally be performed by dental hygienists and registered dental assistants are determined solely by the dentist who is in the office at the time that they are performing those procedures.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE, according to statistics from the American Dental Association Health Policy Institute from a 2013 study?
options: The most common reason given by seniors (adults ages 65 and older) regardless of income level for not going to the dentist is cost.
Fewer than half of all seniors (adults ages 65 and older) actually visited the dentist within the previous year.
Seniors (adults ages 65 and older) with lower household incomes experienced more problems related to the condition of their mouth and teeth.
It is the ethical obligation of the dental profession to work towards alleviating access to dental care issues and related problems that exist for seniors.

questions.text: In the small group sessions we discussed a case in which a nurse suspected that a new patient was an undocumented immigrant and wanted to report the patient to “the appropriate federal authorities.” Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: All US citizens have a duty to report suspected undocumented immigrants because they may be breaking the law.

Even if the doctor did not suspect this individual patient of being an undocumented immigrant, she is not obligated to treat this patient because it is not uncommon for persons of her ethnic group to be undocumented immigrants.
If the doctor began to care for this patient and later found out that she was an undocumented immigrant, she would no longer be obligated to continue treating the patient.
It is permissible to report the patient to “the appropriate federal authorities,” because if the patient committed a crime, she is no longer protected by HIPAA.
The doctor would have an ethical obligation to provide life-saving treatment or stabilization,to the patient if she presented in a life-threatening situation.

questions.text: You encounter a situation in which the ethical way to proceed is not readily apparent. Consider the following statements: I. You should carefully consider how each of the 5 ethical principles we have studied applies to the situation. II. The way to proceed will always immediately become obvious.
options: I is TRUE and II is FALSE.
I is FALSE and II is TRUE.
I and II are both TRUE.
I and II are both FALSE.

questions.text: We discussed a case in which a doctor would be forced to report his patient for not being compliant with the contract he signed to keep his medical appointments, take his medications, and follow health improvement plans. The patient would subsequently lose certain medical benefits. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: The goal of this program was to encourage patients with unhealthy lifestyles to practice responsible self-care and improve their health and decrease medical expenditures by the state.
Well-intentioned programs such as this one may have unintended consequences that are the opposite of what was intended.
In this scenario, the doctor-patient relationship is at risk when the doctor is obligated to report the patient.
Medical costs for the state may end up increasing since that patient loses certain medical benefits and may become sicker and require increased care.
All of these statements are TRUE.

questions.text: When making ethical decisions, a TCDM students may “consider the judgement of others”. Which of the following is not a resource that may be useful?
options: American Dental Association Principles of Ethics and Code of Professional Conduct.
Touro College of Dental Medicine faculty members.
All of the above choices may be useful resources.

questions.text: Consider the following statements: I. In general, a patient below the age of 20, cannot legally give consent for medical or surgical treatments; consent must be obtained from either a parent or a legal guardian. II. There are no exceptions in which consent for medical or surgical procedures can be given by patients under their state’s designated legal age of consent.
options: I is TRUE and II is FALSE.
I is FALSE and II is TRUE.
I and II are both TRUE.
I and II are both FALSE.

questions.text: We discussed a case in which the practice manager in a dental office changed a treatment plan so that teeth would be restored by crowns instead of less extensive restorations, even though the dentist who developed the original treatment plan still believed that restorations, not crowns, were indicated. Consider the following two statements: I. If the dentist provides the crowns as his boss desired even though he does not believe it is the right treatment, this could not be considered unethical as his boss has more experience in treating patients. II. If the dentist provides the crowns, and the patient does not have any increased expenses, no harm was done to the patient so this would not be considered unethical.
options: I is TRUE and II is FALSE.
I is FALSE and II is TRUE.
I and II are both TRUE.
I and II are both FALSE.

questions.text: You share office space with another dentist, but maintain separate practices with your own patients. You believe that you smell alcohol on the other dentist’s breath throughout the day and strongly suspect that he is consuming alcohol between patients and may be impaired while treating patients. Which of the following statements are TRUE?
options: If you are correct, he is violating the ethical principle of autonomy because he might harm his patients.
If you do nothing about this situation, you are not violating the ethical principle of non-maleficence because you bear no ethical responsibility for what happens to his patients in his practice.

Since you are not totally sure he is treating patients while impaired, you are violating the ethical principle of veracity if you approach him about your suspicions because your accusation may not be truthful.
The ethical principle of autonomy allows him to drink alcohol and treat patients as he is allowed to make his own decisions.
None of these statements are TRUE.

questions.text: Your in-person classes have been changed to Zoom sessions due to the COVID-19 pandemic. You are aware that many students are working together on a Zoom quiz by communicating with each other regarding the answers, even though they were told that this was not allowed. You decide to join the group and work with them to determine the answers.  You justify your behavior by reasoning that “everyone else is doing it”, and you “would be at a disadvantage if you did not do it too.” Consider the following statement: The justification described would be a valid ethical argument for defending yourself if you were charged with violating the Honor Code and you would never be found guilty. This statement is:

One of the dentists in your group practice is performing “high-tech” diagnostic procedure on patients for which there is insufficient evidence to support its use. The procedure has not been demonstrated to be as accurate as the traditional “low-tech” treatment. Patients are charged a higher fee for the “high-tech” procedure. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: An inaccurate diagnosis may cause harm to the patient which would be a violation of the ethical principle of non-maleficence.
Not disclosing the potential inaccuracy of the test to the patient would be a violation of the ethical principle of veracity.
Not providing the patient with the information they need to make an informed decision and choose which procedure they would prefer would be a violation of the ethical principle of autonomy.
Charging a higher fee for a less accurate procedure would be a violation of the ethical principle of justice.
All of these statements are TRUE.

questions.text: You have graduated from TCDM and completed a GPR. It is your first day in practice and a patient comes in complaining of pain in their lower jaw and tells you that another dentist had recently completed a crown in that area. The pain they are having is the same pain that they saw the previous dentist for and the crown was done because of that pain. You examine the patient clinically and radiographically and realize that the pain is coming from the tooth next to the one that was treated. When you tell the patient what is going on, they exclaim that their previous dentist was a “quack” and that they want to sue him. Which of the following statements are TRUE?
options: The ethical principle of justice dictates that you cannot assume that the previous dentist did something wrong because you do not know the circumstances that existed when that dentist treated the patient.

You can try to determine the patient’s original condition at the first dentist who is obligated by the ethical principle of autonomy to furnish the patient with a copy of their records if the patient requests those records.
The original dentist cannot provide the records to you without the patient’s permission as this would constitute a HIPAA violation.
The original dentist cannot provide the records to you without the patient’s permission as this would violate patient autonomy.
All of these statements are TRUE.

questions.text: You have graduated from TCDM and completed a GPR. It is your first day in practice and an elderly retired patient comes in with her adult daughter. The patient has an infection. When you tell her she needs antibiotics, she asks you to write the prescription in her daughter’s name, otherwise she will not get it. Her daughter is on a prescription plan but she is not and she can’t afford the prescription. Consider the following statement: Although writing the prescription in her daughter’s name is insurance fraud and is illegal, you cannot get in trouble for doing so because the ethical principle of beneficence outweighs any legal principle. This statement is:
TCDM faculty need to consider the impact of their actions on multiple stakeholders because they have obligations to which of the following groups?
options: TCDM patients, other TCDM faculty, TCDM students, and TCDM/TCUS itself.
TCDM patients, TCDM students, and TCDM/TCUS itself.
TCDM patients, other TCDM faculty, and TCDM students.

questions.text: Two students decide to pull all-nighters to study for a test and decide to take substances to help them stay awake and concentrate. One of the students buys non-prescription No-Doz while the other students gets some prescription Adderall from a friend, even though he has not been prescribed that medication himself. Which of the following statements would be agreed upon by a majority of people as being most accurate?
options: Both students cheated because they used these substances.
Neither student cheated because they still had to take the test based on the knowledge that they acquired.
Any student who takes Adderall, prescribed or not, is a cheater since it gives them an unfair advantage over other students
It doesn’t matter if the students cheated or didn’t cheat, all that matters is that they learned the material.

Like many questions that arise in ethical decision-making, the answer will depend on many factors that need to be considered and may vary from one individual to another based on their background and previous experiences.

questions.text: Now that you have completed this Ethics course and been given the tools to use in ethical decisionmaking, you do not need to take any additional ethics courses during dental school.
Now that you have completed this Ethics course and been given the tools to use in ethical decisionmaking, choosing the most ethical path to take will always be simple.

Consider the following two statements: I. A toll-free Ethics Hotline [(800)621-8099] is available through the American Dental Association to assist its members in managing ethical challenges. II. The Touro College of Dental Medicine SPEA (Student Professionalism and Ethics Association) Chapter is part of a national organization which promotes and support students’ lifelong commitment to ethical behavior in order to benefit the patients they serve and to further the dental profession. Dr. Wachs encourages all students to join this organization.
options: Both of these statements are TRUE.
Neither of these statements is related to anything that was discussed in this course.

questions.text: Which of the following statements as described in The ADA Principles of Ethics and Code of Conduct is FALSE?
options: The ADA Code is, in effect, a written expression of the obligations arising from the implied contract between the dental profession and society.
The ADA Code is an evolving document.
Although ethics and the law are closely related, they are not the same.
Ethical obligations may—and often do—exceed legal duties.
None of the statements here is FALSE.

questions.text: Consider the following five definitions: I. The dentist has a duty to respect the patient’s rights to self-determination and confidentiality.  II. The dentist has a duty to refrain from harming the patient.  III. The dentist has a duty to promote the patient’s welfare.  IV. The dentist has a duty to treat people fairly.  V. The dentist has a duty to communicate truthfully.  Which of the following answer choices includes a list of Ethical Principles correctly ordered to match the definitions above?

The rapid development of the Covid-19 vaccine led to mistrust and hesitancy in some. Which of the following factors did NOT contribute to this successful rapid development of what by all scientific measures has so far proven to be a “safe and effective” vaccine?
options: New platforms for vaccine delivery were already researched.
Rapid gene sequencing of the virus allowed for rapid development of antigen sources.
Vaccine development steps were executed in parallel.
The disease was confined to a very small population so that recruitment for clinical trials was focused on that very small group.
Vaccines were produced in parallel with clinical trials.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an ethical consideration regarding Covid-19 vaccination?
options: Vaccines are available in some parts of the world, but not in others.
People who choose not to get vaccinated pose a threat to others.
Drug companies are offering tiered pricing in different places throughout the world.
Different strategies for education and community engagement are utilized in different places throughout the world.
ALL of the statements here are ethical considerations.

questions.text: Which of the following are NOT ethical obligations of government when dealing with a situation such as the Covid-19 pandemic?
options: To provide honest and effective leadership.
Not to cloud science with politics.
To hide factual information from the public if it conflicts with a policy the government wants to promote.
ALL of the statements here are ethical obligations of government.

questions.text: A school mandates that all of its students must be vaccinated against Covid-19.  Students who are not vaccinated due to legitimate medical reasons cannot attend school. Consider the following three statements: I. This may violate a student’s individual autonomy. II. This may violate a student’s individual veracity. III. This may violate the ethical principles of beneficence and non-maleficence for the individual student but may be consistent with those principles from a health standpoint for the remainder of the school population and their contacts.
options: I, II, and III are TRUE.
Only I and III are TRUE.
Only II and IIII are TRUE.

questions.text: Microaggressions are never intentional, they are always unintentional.
All of the following are effective steps toward becoming an ally towards persons being subjected to microaggressions, EXCEPT:
options: Feeling guilty over past microaggressions you may have committed or witnessed and ignored.
Reflecting on your own advantages and privileges.
Being prepared to see situations differently.
ALL of the statements here are effective steps toward becoming an ally.

questions.text: A microinsult is…
options: …when a person intentionally behaves in a discriminatory manner.
…an action or comment that is unintentionally discriminatory.
…when a person’s comment invalidates or undermines the experiences of a certain group of people.
ALL of these statements describe a microinsult.
NONE of these statements describe a microinsult.

questions.text: Claims that the COVID-19 vaccine causes infertility in women are being spread by so-called experts and many others on social media.  Current science has shown that there is no truth to these claims.  Those falsely promoting these claims are guilty of violating which of the following ethical principles?
Which of the following behaviors is not considered unprofessional behavior for a dental student?
options: Coming to a school social event after hours and getting drunk.
None of the behaviors described here are considered unprofessional.
All of the behaviors described here are considered unprofessional.

questions.text: Consider the following statements: I. It is legitimate to justify “getting around a rule” if you and other reasonable people consider the rule to be non-consequential. II. It is legitimate to justify “getting around a rule” if everyone else is “getting around the rule”. III. It is legitimate to justify “getting around a rule” if you and other reasonable people consider the rule to be nonconsequential and everyone else is “getting around the rule”. IV. Situational ethics can be used to justify getting around a rule.
options: Only I, II, and III are TRUE.
I, II, III, and IV are TRUE.
None of these statements are true.

questions.text: Of the following statements, which one describes the most ethical behavior?
options: Delaying a patient’s treatment so that you can do the procedure on a clinical board examination.
Delaying a patient’s treatment so that you can do the procedure on a clinical board examination when the delay poses no harm to the patient and you obtain the patient’s consent.
Delaying a patient’s treatment so that you can do the procedure on a clinical board examination when the delay poses no harm to the patient.
Delaying a patient’s treatment so that you can do the procedure on a clinical board examination when you obtain the patient’s consent.
NONE of these behaviors can be described as ethical.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an obligation of TCDM faculty to their students?
options: To inform students of criteria that will be used for evaluation prior to the evaluation.
To stay current in teaching techniques even if there has been no change in the information being presented for many years.
To maintain ZERO tolerance for cheating and dishonesty.
To place student learning ahead of patient care.
To maintain student privacy and confidentiality.

questions.text: When assessing a situation to determine the most ethical way to proceed, all of the following steps must be taken EXCEPT:
options: Identify the perspective of all stakeholders
Choose a solution that satisfies all ethical principles.

questions.text: Consider the following two statements: I. A licensed, practicing dentist must put the interest of their patients ahead of her/his own interests. II. A dental student can put her/his own interests ahead of their patient’s interests as the student needs to learn all of the skills involved in the practice of dentistry.
options: I and II are both NOT TRUE.

questions.text: Consider the following statements: I. The original Hippocratic Oath includes a physician’s duty to protect patient privacy/confidentiality. II. The Modern Hippocratic Oath includes a physician’s duty to protect patient privacy/confidentiality. III. HIPAA laws include a physician’s duty to protect patient privacy/confidentiality.
options: I, II, and III are all TRUE.
Only I and III are TRUE.
Only II and III are TRUE.

questions.text: The ADA Principles of Ethics and Code of Professional Conduct include all of the following, EXCEPT:
options: A description of the principles of ethics which includes aspirational goals of the profession.
A Code of Professional Conduct that expresses specific conducts that are required or prohibited.
Advisory Opinions that consist of interpretations applying the Code of Professional Conduct to specific situations.
A statement that high ethical standards should be adopted and practiced throughout the dental school educational process.
A description of specific situations in which ethical behavior can be suspended.

questions.text: Consider the following statements: I. A dentist must provide emergency care to their patients of record. II. A dentist cannot criticize the work of other dentists. III. A dentist can only provide expert testimony if it is just and fair. IV. A dentist can split fees with other dentists but not with medical doctors. When considering the ethical principle of justice…
options: …only I and IV are TRUE when considering the ethical principle of justice.
…only  I and III are TRUE when considering the ethical principle of justice.
…only I, III, and IV are TRUE when considering the ethical principle of justice.
…only I, II, and III are TRUE when considering the ethical principle of justice.
…I, II, III, and IV are all TRUE when considering the ethical principle of justice.

questions.text: A patient that you are in the midst of treating makes statements that you consider offensive and you wish to dismiss them from your practice. Consider the following two statements: I. Dismissing the patient violates the principle of patient autonomy as the patient cannot continue care with their chosen provider. II. Dismissing the patient promotes patient autonomy if you are concerned that you may now treat the patient differently because of unconscious or implicit bias and the patient should be able to choose a provider who will treat them properly.
options: I and II are both TRUE.
I and II are both NOT TRUE.
I is TRUE and II is NOT TRUE.
I is NOT TRUE and II is TRUE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about healthcare is FALSE?
options: Healthcare can be considered a fundamental social good that promotes human dignity and well-being.
Healthcare is an individual right guaranteed to all Americans in the Constitution.
Healthcare can be considered a communal obligation.
Healthcare can be considered a commodity.
NONE of these statements is FALSE.

questions.text: Access to medical care may be hindered by:
options: Utilizing inaccurate race-based corrections of laboratory findings.
Lack of medical insurance or funds to pay for medical care.
Differing approaches to provision of care by physicians vs. hospital facilities.
Conflicts between a physician’s obligation to an individual patient vs. society.

questions.text: Health inequities are differences in health status or in the distribution of health resources between different population groups, arising from the social conditions in which people are born, grow, live, work, and age.  Which of the following parameters can be used as a measure of health inequities?
options: All of these choices can be used as a measure of health inequities.

questions.text: Structural Determinants of Health are social variables that impact a person’s health. They include all of the following EXCEPT:
options: The neighborhood, community, and physical environment where a person lives.
The presence of genes that are responsible for various diseases in a given person.

questions.text: The Weathering Hypothesis is stated in which of the following?
options: African Americans experience early health deterioration as a consequence of the cumulative impact of repeated experience with social or economic adversity and political marginalization.

Deterioration in the health status of individuals occurs in persons subjected to weather extremes due to an inadequate housing situation and/or economic status which makes them unable to limit their exposure to these extremes.
A person will not be able to improve their health if they do not have an economic stake in making this improvement occur.
Individuals can control all factors affecting their health except their genetic makeup.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: Federal laws govern how you practice with specific laws directed at healthcare operations such as HIPAA.
The specific procedures you are allowed to perform in practice are governed by state laws.
Local municipality laws may affect how you practice with laws such as zoning regulations.
A license to practice dentistry is granted by the federal government.
ALL of these statements are TRUE.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an example of a HIPAA violation?
options: A dentist posting his schedule with patients’ names and the procedures they will be undergoing in a location where other patients can see it.
A dentist posting his schedule with no patient names on it but only with the procedures he/she will be doing in a location where other patients can see it.
A dentist leaving a message with a patient’s relative with specific health-related information without the patient’s permission.
A dentist speaking with a representative of the patient’s insurance provider to get preapproval for a necessary procedure.
All of these statements are examples of HIPAA violations.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is most accurate?
options: The age of consent is always 21, the same as for buying alcohol.
The age of consent is always 18, the same as for voting.
The age of consent is generally 18 but may in certain instances be lowered to 13 if the patient is deemed to have adequate cognition and maturity.
The age of consent is always 16, the same as for driving.
The age of consent is 18 for males and 16 for females since females mature earlier.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: Disgruntled employees are often a source of complaints reported to the Office of Professional Discipline.
Unhappy patients are often a source of complaints reported to the Office of Professional Discipline.
The Office of Professional Discipline is required to investigate any complaints about dentists that it receives.
You should deal with Office of Professional Discipline investigations on your own because hiring a lawyer will make it look like you know you are guilty of wrongdoing.
You should not invite Office of Professional Discipline investigators into your office.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding fee accommodations is FALSE?
options: A dentist can make fee accommodations for patients on a case-by-case basis.
A dentist cannot make fee accommodations that are discriminatory.
A dentist can make fee accommodations for a specific group such as all members of the clergy.
A dentist can make fee accommodations for clergy members of just one faith.
A dentist can make fee accommodations for all patients by just accepting what insurance pays and not collecting co-pays or deductibles.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about dismissing a patient from a dental practice if FALSE?
options: Specific rules dictate the conditions for dismissing a patient from a dental practice.
If a patient is not dismissed in a manner consistent with stated regulations, the dentist is guilty of patient abandonment.
In New York State, if a patient is dismissed from a practice, the dismissing dentist is required to continue to provide care for 180 days.
A patient cannot be dismissed from a practice if they are a member of a protected class or if the dismissal is discriminatory.
All of these statements are TRUE.

questions.text: You were presented with a case where a patient did not want their current dentist to tell their new dentist about a medical issue that the patient had which required antibiotics prior to dental care.  The patient was switching dentists to avoid taking the antibiotics even though not taking the antibiotics could be life-threatening. Which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: The principle of non-maleficence supports the current dentist going against the patient’s wishes and informing the new dentist about the patient medical issue.
It may be illegal for the current dentist to go against the patient’s wishes and inform the new dentist about the patient medical issue.
The principle of beneficence supports the current dentist doing what is possible and clinically appropriate so that the patient receives premedication when necessary.

The principle of beneficence supports the current dentist complying with the expressed desires of the patient. It states that the dentist must act “within the bounds of clinical circumstances presented by the patient, with due consideration being given to the needs, desires and values of the patient.”
ALL of these statements are TRUE.

questions.text: You were presented with a case where a patient requested sub-standard care that would be covered by their insurance and offered to sign a waiver absolving the dentist from responsibility if the treatment did not work. Which of the following statements is most accurate?
options: The dentist has no choice but to comply with the patient’s request as required by the principle of patient autonomy.
If the dentist performs the requested treatment this would violate the principle of nonmaleficence.

Since the requested sub-standard treatment would be covered by insurance and all of the other options would not be covered, the dentist can justify doing substandard treatment by invoking the principle of beneficence since from a financial perspective, this is then in the patient’s best interest.

The dentist should explain everything to the patient again and say that the requested treatment may not be optimal but it “really isn’t sub-standard” and then the dentist should perform that treatment.
The dentist can perform the sub-standard treatment by rationalizing that the patient would just go to another dentist who will do the requested procedure.

questions.text: You were presented with a case where a recently graduated dentist had his treatment plans changed to what they felt was unnecessary and more complex treatment by the practice manager, who was the wife of the dentist owner and was not a dentist herself.  The recent grad was worried that if they did not implement the revised treatment plan, they may lose their job. Consider the following statement:  If the owner dentist insists on this new treatment plan and the young dentist feels it can harm the patient, the young dentist is obligated for the patient’s sake to bring the matter to the attention of the local constituent or component dental society.

You were presented with a case in which a dentist told a patient to sue their previous dentist so the patient could then afford the “good dentistry” that the new dentist would provide. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: A difference of opinion as to preferred treatment should not be communicated to the patient in a manner which would unjustly imply mistreatment.
Dentists are obligated under the ADA Code to report any “instances of gross or continual faulty treatment by other dentists” to the appropriate agencies.
Advising the patient to hold off on necessary treatment until they win their suit may be an ethical violation because dentists are obligated to provide competent and timely delivery of dental care.
ALL of these statements are TRUE.
ALL of these statements are FALSE.

questions.text: You were presented with a case in which a dentist was concerned about his long-term friend and partner’s apparent drug dependency. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: If a dentist is practicing while impaired, they can potentially harm a patient in violation of the principle of autonomy.
A dentist bears no responsibility to act when they feel another dentist is endangering the welfare of a patient.

A dentist with first-hand knowledge of a colleague’s impairment is ethically responsible to report the colleague to the professional assistance or chemical dependency committee of the appropriate dental society.
A dentist who is impaired is obligated to report this impairment to all patients that they have ever treated.
The concerned dentist should observe the impaired partner when they are providing treatment but they only need to act if they know that the patient is being harmed.

questions.text: You were presented with a case in which a participant in a research study wanted to be “reimbursed” for transportation costs that she did not actually incur. When analyzing this case, which of the following questions is legitimate to consider?
options: Could the transportation “reimbursement” be construed by some as a payment for participating in the study and thus be a form of coercion?
Could “reimbursing” the participant for a cost that she did not incur compromise the research?
Is there an ethical concern with the study director agreeing to “reimburse” the participant when that is not an honest description of what occurred?
Does it matter who made the decision to “reimburse” the participant?
ALL of these questions are legitimate to consider.

questions.text: You were presented with a case in which a patient presented to a clinic with what appeared to be fake ID and members of the clinic staff suspected that the patient was an undocumented immigrant and wanted to turn her in to immigration authorities. Which of the following statements regarding the LEGAL considerations in this case is/are FALSE?
options: Even if there was proof that the ID was fake and the patient was in the US illegally, clinic personnel are not legally required to turn her in as there is no general obligation to report a crime.

The clinic has no legal responsibility to verify the patient’s identity when they suspect identity fraud and can bill the insurance provider under the name and insurance information that the patient provided.

If the clinic doctor reasonably concludes that they will be unable to treat the patient safely because the patient is likely to withhold or misrepresent important information, the doctor can legally decline to enter into the doctor-patient relationship from the start.

The doctor cannot legally refuse to care for the patient on the basis of her membership in a legally protected category—for example, race, religion, national origin, color, sex/gender/gender identity/sexual orientation, veteran status, or disability.

All the personal information the patient provided—her name, her address, and any other data such as her health history and current complaint—is protected from disclosure to immigration authorities under the HIPAA laws.

questions.text: You were presented with a case in which a patient presented to a clinic with what appeared to be fake ID and members of the clinic staff suspected that the patient was an undocumented immigrant and wanted to turn her in. Which of the following statements regarding the ETHICAL considerations in this case is/are FALSE?
options: The principle of beneficence would be consistent with a belief that the duty of a physician is to take care of anyone who comes to him or her for care, regardless of that person’s societal status.
A physician has a moral obligation to work for free.
A physician has a professional obligation to leave prejudices at home.

If the physician was legally bound to report patients with suspicious immigration status, an argument could be made that the demands of beneficence and the weight of the patient-doctor relationship can transcend the law, and the physician would be morally justified if they chose not to report.
ALL of these statements are FALSE.

questions.text: You were presented with a case in which a patient’s medical benefits were reduced because the patient smoked tobacco. Which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: Physicians may see conflicts between their legal and ethical duties if they are required to report a patient who smokes.
Patients may be unfairly penalized because failure to achieve the goal of not smoking does not necessarily mean that the patient was noncompliant with a smoking cessation program.

Reposition the fragment and stabilize with sutures.

questions.text: A patient develops a severe dull ache in the jaw four days after a dental extraction. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: The most likely etiology is loss of the alveolar blood clot.
Narcotic analgesics are necessary for pain relief.
The most likely etiology is exposure of cementum of an adjacent tooth.
The tooth should be put back in so the patient feels better.

questions.text: Hemorrhage after dental procedures can be prevented by or treated by:
options: Identifying and treating systemic bleeding issues.
Performing careful surgery including atraumatic reflection of mucoperiosteal flaps.

questions.text: You are extracting a lower right third molar with pericoronitis that is in close proximity to the inferior alveolar nerve. You have almost completely delivered the tooth from the socket, but a piece of the distal root has fractured off. What do you do?
options: If the piece of root is greater than 2mm and close to the inferior alveolar nerve, it should be left in place and monitored.
If the piece of root is less than 2mm and close to the inferior alveolar nerve, it should be left in place and monitored.
The piece of root must be removed, despite the risk of injuring the inferior alveolar nerve.
The piece of root should be reduced in size with a handpiece to less than 4mm and retained in the socket for monitoring.
Manipulation with an elevator might accidentally displace the root into the inferior alveolar nerve canal or through the lingual plate, so the root should be obliterated with a large round bur.

questions.text: You have extracted a lower left third molar on a 21 year-old male. The socket won't stop bleeding after you have applied pressure for ten minutes. You maintain good suction and identify the source of bleeding as directly from the bone marrow. You are able to see an intact bony socket without any exposure of the inferior alveolar nerve. What is the next step?
options: Pack with gauze again and apply pressure only.
Pack with gelfoam or Surgicel, apply pressure, then suture the socket.
Irrigate the socket copiously, suture, and discharge the patient.
Send the patient to the hospital for angiography and embolization.
Give the patient anti-hypertensive medication to lower their blood pressure so that the bleeding will stop.

questions.text: You are extracting a palatally inclined upper right third molar. Despite having a throat pack in place, while you are delivering the tooth the patient coughs, and the tooth disappears. Now what?
options: Check that the patient is still responsive and breathing comfortably.
Carefully remove the throat pack and see if the tooth is somewhere in the throat pack.
Inform the patient of what may have happened with the tooth - that it may have entered their GI or respiratory tract.
Send the patient to the emergency room for evaluation including chest/abdominal radiographs to locate tooth.

questions.text: An 8-year-old presents with a pulp exposure due to a traumatic crown fracture on a permanent central incisor. You determine the pulpal and periapical diagnosis to be healthy. The root is not completely formed. The best procedure here is:

An adult patient presents to your office with recent trauma to his front teeth. Periapical radiograph shows a horizontal root fracture of tooth #9 in the apical third of the root. The tooth should be splinted for:
What is the recommended treatment for a horizontal root fracture?
options: Always perform root canal therapy to the apex (both coronal and apical segments).
Always perform root canal therapy up to the fracture line.
Always perform root canal in the apical segment only.
Always perform root canal therapy of the coronal segment and extract the apical segment.
Any treatment, including possible root canal therapy, will be dictated by the location of the fracture and other specifics regarding the tooth injury and current status.

questions.text: A patient presents with a subluxation injury to tooth #9. The best treatment is:
Which luxation injury is usually associated with an alveolar fracture?
Because the prognosis for most intrusive luxation injuries is favorable, the treatment of choice is to monitor and follow up rather than root canal therapy.
A patient calls to say her front tooth was knocked out. She has the tooth in her hand. The best thing you can tell her is:
options: Place the tooth in a cup of water and bring it to the office immediately.
Place the tooth in a cup of milk and bring it to the office within the next couple hours.
Place the tooth in a cup of milk and bring it to the office immediately.
Give the tooth to the tooth fairy and use the money you receive to pay for an implant.
Scrub the tooth with soap and water and bring it to the office in the morning when she feels better.

questions.text: If an avulsed tooth was replanted after being out of the socket for an extended period of time, the most likely outcome is:
All forms of root resorption are amenable to root canal therapy.
The treatment of choice for pulp canal obliteration (calcification) after trauma is root canal therapy:
Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding the treatment of traumatized PRIMARY TEETH?
options: Avulsed primary teeth should be replanted within 3 hours of the avulsion.
Laterally luxated primary teeth that have been severely displaced should be repositioned and splinted for 2 weeks.
Laterally luxated primary teeth that have been severely displaced should be repositioned and splinted for 8 weeks.
Palatally displaced intruded primary teeth should be observed and allowed to spontaneously re-erupt.
Facially displaced intruded primary teeth should be observed and allowed to spontaneously re-erupt.

questions.text: Which of the following signs or symptoms may be indicative of devitalization of a primary tooth that has been traumatized in the past?
options: Fistula on the gingiva overlying the root.
Swelling of the gingiva overlying the root.

questions.text: Greater than 50% of physical trauma in child abuse happens in the head and neck region.
Which are the most frequently traumatized teeth?

options: Make sure the patient is stable.
Obtain a comprehensive history and physical.
Locate any foreign bodies with radiographic imaging.

options: Reposition, semi-rigid splint, and evaluation and follow by endodontist.
Reposition, rigid splint, and evaluation and follow by endodontist.

options: Reposition, soft diet and NSAIDs and no further treatment.

questions.text: Case Scenario: Congratulations!  You have successfully completed your OMFS Residency and have just opened your own office. PMH was significant for: Crohn’s disease Insulin dependent diabetes (IDDM) Osteoporosis DVT (deep vein thrombosis) Vaso-vagal episodes with medical procedures Medications: Insulin regimen –sliding scale as follows: Regular and NPH titrated Prednisone - 60 mg po daily for one month Fosamax –70 mg once per week Warfarin –5 and 10 mg alternating daily Examination: Non-restorable, carious roots –18/19/30 17 –severe distal cervical caries, deemed to be non-restorable Missing –31/32 No swelling/fistula No trismus Moderate expansion of the right posterior mandible Panoramic radiograph: See below. You inform the patient about the lesion of the right mandible and her need for treatment of this lesion.  You explain that her ultimate treatment will depend on the histopathologic diagnosis.  You consult her physician regarding her medical history, medications, and proposed treatment. At your request, he checks her INR 3 days prior to treatment and reports a value of 1.8. Which of the following is a reasonable initial treatment for the lesion that you and the physician agree on?
options: Perform an excisional biopsy after discontinuing the warfarin for 3 days.
Perform an excisional biopsy without interrupting the warfarin therapy.
Perform an incisional biopsy after discontinuing the warfarin for 3 days.
Perform an incisional biopsy without interrupting the warfarin therapy.
Remove the entire lesion after discontinuing the warfarin for 3 days.

“Shift to the left” showing high number of young, immature white blood cells

questions.text: Consider the following statements: I. An unerupted tooth is a tooth whose crown has not come through the gingival tissue into the oral cavity. II. An impacted tooth is a tooth that has not erupted into the oral cavity within normal range of expected time. III. All Impacted teeth must be surgically exposed or removed. IV. All unerupted teeth must be surgically exposed or removed. Which of the following choices is correct?
options: I, II, III, and IV are all TRUE.
I, II, III, and IV are all FALSE.
I and IV are TRUE and II and III are FALSE.
I, II and IV are TRUE and III is FALSE.
I and II are TRUE and III and IV are FALSE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding factors associated with tooth impaction are FALSE?
options: Systemic factors can result in the impaction of multiple teeth.
Cleidocranial dysplasia can be a factor associated with tooth impaction.
Local factors may result in tooth impaction.
Odontogenic cysts or tumors can result in tooth impaction.
If a tooth is impacted due to systemic factors, it cannot be extracted.

questions.text: Which of the following endings to the following sentence is most accurate? If an impacted tooth remains asymptomatic and does not develop pathology by the time a patient reaches the age of 35…
options: …it will never need to be extracted.
…it should be removed as soon as possible since, as the patient gets older, the extraction and recovery become more difficult.
…continued observation is indicated since, as the patient gets older, the extraction and recovery become easier.
…it should be followed clinically and radiographically to see if it becomes problematic.
……it should be removed as soon as possible since, as the patient gets older, extraction would be accompanied by increased risk of complications.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the Pell and Gregory classification system is TRUE?
options: It is useful because it gives an indication as to the anticipated difficulty of the extraction.
The classification is utilized by insurance companies to determine what the fee should be.
1, 2, and 3 classifications are based on the depth of the third molar relative to the adjacent second molar.
A, B, and C classifications are based on the buccolingual diameter of the third molar.
It is useful in describing the position of any tooth that is impacted.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the prognostic value of panoramic radiography of inferior alveolar nerve damage after mandibular third molar removal is FALSE?
options: Interruption of the superior cortical border of the Inferior Alveolar Canal is indicative of increased risk.
Deflection of the Inferior Alveolar Canal is indicative of increased risk.
Narrowing of the Inferior Alveolar Canal is indicative of increased risk.
Darkening of the tooth root where it overlies the Inferior Alveolar Canal is indicative of decreased risk.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the use of CBCT’s prior to third molar extractions is TRUE?
options: CBCT is required prior to extraction of all mandibular third molars.
CBCT is required prior to extraction of all maxillary third molars.
CBCT is required prior to extraction of all maxillary and mandibular third molars.
CBCT is never useful prior to extraction of any third molars.
All of the statements other than this one are NOT TRUE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding flap design for the extraction of mandibular third molars is TRUE?
options: The flap should be a full-thickness flap and it should flare to the buccal in the area posterior to the adjacent second molar.
The flap should be a split-thickness flap and it should flare to the lingual in the area posterior to the adjacent second molar.
The flap should be a split-thickness flap and it should flare to the buccal in the area posterior to the adjacent second molar.
The flap should be a full-thickness flap and it should flare to the lingual in the area posterior to the adjacent second molar.

Buccal bone should be removed for access to the crown.
The second molar must be removed to gain access to the third molar.
Both buccal and lingual bone should be removed for access to the crown.

questions.text: You have made the decision to section this tooth to accomplish the extraction. Which of the following statements is TRUE?

To avoid damaging the buccal nerve, you do not cut completely through the buccal surface of the tooth.
To avoid damaging the lingual nerve, you do not cut completely through the lingual surface of the tooth.

You cut completely through the tooth from buccal to lingual to remove the crown.

Distoangular positioned teeth are generally the most difficult to extract.

options: It is not necessary to provide any information to an Oral and Maxillofacial Pathologist about a lesion or patient, because a good Oral and Maxillofacial Pathologist only cares about what she/he sees when looking at a specimen under the microscope.
Microscopic examination of different areas of the same lesion might yield different diagnoses.
A general pathologist can make as accurate a diagnosis of odontogenic lesions as an Oral and Maxillofacial Pathologist.

If a dentist advises a patient of the need for biopsy of a potentially dangerous oral lesion and the patient does not follow-up, the dentist bears no responsibility to attempt to have the patient obtain treatment.
If you observe a lesion whose appearance is highly suspicious of malignancy and the specimen is read as benign, you do not need to re-evaluate or follow the lesion.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about cystic lesions is FALSE?
options: Enucleation of a cystic lesion is often performed as an excisional biopsy and no further treatment is necessary.
The existence of a cleavage layer where fibrous connective tissue meets bone enables enucleation by curettage.
Large cysts may “push” nerves and blood vessels to the side.
Marsupialization may decrease the risk of damage to vital structures by allowing a cystic lesion to shrink prior to excision.
Once marsupialization of a cystic lesion is performed, no further treatment will be necessary.

questions.text: Which of the following characteristics of a lesion should be considered when determining what management is indicated?
options: Pace of growth of the lesion.
Proximity of the lesion to vital structures.

questions.text: Which of these lesions does NOT require composite resection?

Consider the following statements. I. The sublingual space is located inferior to the mylohyoid muscle. II. Infection located in the sublingual space can travel around the free border of the mylohyoid muscle to enter the submandibular space. III. Infection located in the sublingual space can present clinically as a raised tongue. IV. The submandibular space does not communicate with the sublingual space.
options: I, II, and III are TRUE.

questions.text: The pterygomandibular raphe serves as an anatomical landmark when administering local anesthetic for an inferior alveolar nerve block. This raphe represents the joining of which two muscles?
options: Orbicularis oris and superior pharyngeal constrictor.
Orbicularis oris and the middle pharyngeal constrictor.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about infections related to partially impacted third molars is FALSE?
options: Pericoronitis describes a painful condition of an inflamed, swollen operculum overlying the coronal portion of a third molar.
Long-term resolution of pericoronitis can be predictably accomplished by either extraction of the involved tooth, or operculectomy, excision of the tissue overlying the tooth.
An arcuate zone of radiolucency posterior to a mandibular third molar is indicative of bone loss due to chronic infection.
Measures such as local curettage and antibacterial rinses may allow for resolution of acute pericoronitis.
Removal of the etiology of the pericoronitis is necessary to predictably prevent continued recurrences.

questions.text: Which of the following clinical signs are NOT indicative of advanced infection?
options: All of the clinical signs listed here are indicative of advanced infection.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about incision and drainage procedures are FALSE?
options: Incision and drainage of an abscess can be effective as it allows release of purulence from the abscess.
Incision and drainage of a cellulitis can be effective as it changes the anaerobic environment by allowing oxygen into the site.
If a successful incision and drainage procedure is performed, i.e. copious amounts of purulence are obtained, culture and sensitivity studies ae not necessary.
Drains should be placed to allow continued drainage of any additional purulence that develops.
Gram stain of the purulence may be helpful as it narrows the list of likely causative organisms immediately.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding incision and drainage procedures is FALSE?
options: Blunt dissection techniques will reduce the risk of damaging nerves.
Blunt dissection techniques will reduce the risk of damaging blood vessels.
Incision sites for extraoral incision and drainage procedures should be selected to minimize noticeable scarring whenever possible.
Incision sites for extraoral incision and drainage procedures should be positioned superior to the abscess so that the purulence is drawn away from the airway.
None of these statements is FALSE.

questions.text: A patient presents to you several days after tooth #8 being avulsed and replanted. The tooth also had a crown fracture which exposed the root canal space. The most important factor in terms of long term prognosis for this tooth is:
As a general rule, we manage the pulp the same way after a traumatic injury no matter the age of the patient.
Intrusive luxation injuries tend to also have an associated alveolar fracture.

A patient presents with a history of trauma 3 months previously. Upon radiographic examination you notice that tooth #10 has a significant periapical lesion. You also notice that the root is not completely formed (open apex). The best treatment for this tooth would be:

A patient presents with a history of trauma 3 months previously. Upon radiographic examination you notice that tooth #10 has a significant periapical lesion. You also notice that the root is not completely formed (open apex). You would expect a tooth like this to have a negative response to your vitality testing (cold test).
Horizontal root fractures after trauma ALWAYS need to be treated endodontically (root canal therapy).
The major difference on examination between a tooth concussion injury and a subluxation injury is that one of these is percussion sensitive while the other is not.
All of the following are potential negative sequelae to the permanent dentition after primary tooth trauma EXCEPT:
Consider the following two statements: For a primary tooth root fracture… I. …coronal fragments should be extracted. II. …removal of non-infected apical fragments should be avoided.
options: I is TRUE and II is FALSE.
I is FALSE and II is TRUE.

questions.text: A 26 year-old male was playing hockey without a proper mask and was hit in the mouth with a puck. On examination, teeth 4, 5, and 6 have mobility, moving together when any of the teeth are pushed individually. They are NOT separately mobile and move almost as an entire segment. The remainder of the oral/dental examination is within normal limits. Which of the following statements are TRUE?
options: You diagnose this as luxation of teeth 4, 5, 6 and place a semi-rigid composite splint.
You diagnose this as an alveolar fracture, digitally reduce the segment and check occlusion. Then you place a rigid splint for fixation.
You diagnose this as luxation of teeth 4, 5, 6 and an alveolar fracture so you place a composite splint spanning across teeth 2-8 and a rigid splint from 2-15.
You diagnose this as intrusion and luxation of teeth 4, 5, 6 and place a composite semi-rigid splint across teeth 4, 5, 6.

questions.text: A 33 year-old male presents to your office after a minor motor vehicle accident. He refused to be seen in the hospital prior to coming to you, mostly concerned about his “front tooth” that was fractured. On examination, you note that tooth 9 has a class III fracture (with fractured enamel, dentin, pulp). The most important question(s) you ask this patient is which of the following?
options: What was the manner of the motor vehicle accident? Did the airbag deploy? Did you lose consciousness when you hit the steering wheel/airbag?
How does the tooth feel? Can I take a radiograph?
Does it feel like any other teeth were affected?
Was there anyone else in the car who was injured?
Where were you going when this occurred?

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: Fractures of the alveolar process occur most frequently in the mandibular molar regions.
When dealing with alveolar process fractures, early reduction and stabilization is most important.
Alveolar process fractures take 10-14 days to heal with non-rigid stabilization.
After an alveolar process fracture heals, you do not need to address the associated teeth.
Alveolar fractures can only occur in one jaw in a given patient.

questions.text: A 46 year-old female presents to your office for extraction of tooth 12. It was previously endodontically treated with post/core and pfm crown. The pfm crown has fractured and is loosely attached to the remainder of the tooth root. The tooth also has a periapical radiolucent lesion with an associated draining fistula on the palate. You attempt to extract the tooth surgically – raising a flap and using a handpiece to trough the buccal aspect and find a purchase. However, the tooth continues to fracture until you have less than 2mm of the dilacerated palatal root remaining. Note that the tooth apex is not proximal to the maxillary sinus. What is your next step?
options: Retrieve the entirety of the root surgically and curette the granulomatous tissue from the area corresponding to the periapical radiolucency
Leave the root in place to avoid any further complications.
Tell the patient that you are going to leave the root fragment in place today and retrieve it in another 6 months once it has erupted more
Drill as much of the tooth root down so that it is less than 1mm in size, and then it is okay to leave it.

questions.text: Which of the following spaces is the MOST DANGEROUS for a tooth to be displaced to?
The most common site for an oral antral communication is the maxillary third molar site.

You are extracting stand-alone, erupted tooth 16 on a 59 year-old male. You administer local anesthesia and begin to gently elevate the tooth. While you are elevating the tooth, you hear a loud crack. What do you do next?
options: Continue to elevate and extract the tooth. A crack is part of the normal sounds you would hear when extracting any tooth.
Check to see if the maxillary tuberosity is still intact. If it has fractured, you just continue to perform the extraction as usual and just remove it if it comes with the tooth.

Check to see if the maxillary tuberosity is still intact. If it has fractured, you gently dissect the soft tissue off around it and deliver it with the tooth atraumatically. You then smooth any sharp bony ridges and suture any mucosal tears.
Check to see if there’s an oral antral communication. If there is, you continue to extract the tooth as you usually would and leave the socket open to heal by secondary intention.

questions.text: A 78 year-old male presents for extraction of stand-alone tooth 2. The sinus is severely pneumatized on both the distal and mesial aspects. You perform the extraction surgically, raising a flap and using a surgical handpiece.  However, you realize that an oral antral communication occurs and you treat it correctly, as follows:
options: The oral antral communication is <2mm, so you opt to perform a buccal fat pad graft to achieve primary closure.
The oral antral communication is somewhere between 3-6mm, so you place a solitary suture over the site for closure.
The oral antral communication is >6mm, so you perform a tension free primary closure and instruct the patient to follow strict sinus precautions for the following 6-8 weeks.
The oral antral communication is <2mm, so you do not suture it but you do instruct the patient to follow strict sinus precautions for the following 6-8 weeks.
The oral antral communication is 3-6mm, so you don’t tell the patient and if he notices it later, you tell him it was his fault for not following the post-op instructions.

questions.text: Consider the following two statements: I. It is fairly common and acceptable to have a thermal/rotary injury to the lip from a bur/handpiece. II. A throat screen is only necessary when you are extracting posterior teeth.
options: I and II are both TRUE.
I and II are both FALSE.
I is TRUE and II is FALSE.

I is FALSE and II is TRUE. CONSIDER THE CASE SCENARIO DESCRIBED BELOW WHEN ANSWERING QUESTIONS 43 -50, FOLLOWING THE CASE. You need to take care of this now because, nothing personal, I hate the dentist, and I am NOT coming back.” Denies any other oral/dental symptoms or pain. Medical history: PMH: Diabetes Hypertension Anxiety disorder Severe medical/dental phobia Previous fibroids Hyperthyroid GIRD Elevated cholesterol PSH: Hysterectomy 13 years ago Medications: Famotidine (histamine-2 blocker) 20 mg daily Synthroid (thyroid hormone) 150 mcg daily Metoprolol (beta-blocker) 25 mg daily Metformin (oral hypoglycemic) 500 mg TID Atorvastatin (statin) 40 mg daily Aspirin 81 mg daily Alprazolam (anxiolytic) Takes .5 mg prn anxiety Allergies: NKDA Social: Smokes 3 ppd (packs per day) cigarettes daily for 40 years Drinks 1 bottle of wine daily Vital Signs: BP: 150/91 HR: 55 Oral exam: Dental exam: #19 – PFM with fractured porcelain on lingual surface with extremely sharp edges. Radiograph:

questions.text: The statement printed in RED above is the:
Which of the following statements is MOST ACCURATE?
options: The patient’s pulse is considered NORMAL because it is between the low and high normal limits of 50-80.
The patient’s pulse is considered SLOW because it is NOT between the low and high normal limits of 60-110.
The patient’s pulse is considered SLOW because it is NOT between the low and high normal limits of 60-100.
The patient’s pulse is considered SLOW because it is NOT between the low and high normal limits of 70-110.
The patient’s pulse is considered FAST because it is NOT between the low and high normal limits of 20-50.

questions.text: What is the most likely reason for the patient’s current heart rate of 55?
options: This is a trick question - this is a normal heart rate.

questions.text: Given the patient’s medical history, the procedure can be performed at the patient’s current blood pressure.
You note the lesion on the left lateral border of the tongue. What is your plan?
options: The diagnosis is traumatic ulcer so plan to smooth the edges on the sharp PFM crown on tooth 19. No follow up is required.

You come up with a differential that includes a spectrum of traumatic ulcer (from sharp pfm tooth 19) to possible squamous cell carcinoma (secondary to her social history). You plan to extract tooth 19 today, and at the same time (since she will already be numb), you will take an incisional biopsy of the tongue lesion.
You diagnose this lesion as squamous cell carcinoma and immediately discuss this with the patient and refer her directly to a head and neck oncologist.
You diagnose this lesion as a traumatic ulcer and plan to extract tooth 19 (with sharp pfm crown) today. You tell the patient this lesion will go away. No follow up is required.

You come up with a differential that includes a spectrum of traumatic ulcer (from sharp pfm tooth 19) to possible squamous cell carcinoma (secondary to her social history). You plan to extract tooth 19 today, and have the patient return in two months to see if the lesion has resolved.

questions.text: Do you consider the extraction of tooth 19 to be complicated or uncomplicated?

You perform the extraction of tooth 19 on this patient during your first visit. Despite her dislike of the dentist, she follows up two weeks later. She reports that the lesion is still there and still painful. What is your next step?
options: Immediately refer the patient to the oral & maxillofacial surgeon
Prescribe her a topical steroid mouthrinse to help reduce the inflammation more quickly and assure her that it will go away in time
Begin to assess her other lower left lingual cusps for sharp edges and smooth them out.
Prescribe her an antifungal mouthrinse (nystatin) and tell her that she must have a traumatic ulcer with an overlying fungal infection.
Give her a night guard so she stops biting her tongue. BONUS QUESTIONS:

questions.text: THIS BONUS QUESTION CAN EARN YOU 1 EXTRA POINT: The patient returns to your office 10 days following the extraction of# 19.  They are complaining of tooth pain and facial swelling. Extraoral examination reveals facial asymmetry with fluctuant swelling over the left mandibular body, as well as inferior to the mandible. Intraoral exam reveals swelling in the left floor of the mouth with raised tongue. You are concerned because you suspect:
options: The patient has an infection of the infraorbital space which could lead to cavernous sinus thrombosis
The patient has an infection of the infraorbital space which can travel to the mediastinum.
The patient has an abscess of the sublingual and submandibular spaces which could compromise the airway
The patient has an abscess contained to the buccal space.
The patient has a dry socket.
