options: Pericoronitis is a very pleasant condition.
Perry Allman is a very pleasant individual who did a great job as your class rep and everyone should thank him.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about accidental tooth displacement is TRUE?
options: If a tooth is displaced into the floor of the mouth, it should be left there until fibrosis occurs so it becomes easier to retrieve.
If a tooth is displaced into the infratemporal fossa, antibiotics should be prescribed only if acute infection was present prior to the extraction.
The mandibular third molar is the tooth most commonly displaced into the infratemporal fossa.
When elevating a full-thickness flap to retrieve a tooth or root displaced into the floor of the mouth, there is a high risk of damage to the inferior alveolar nerve.
None of these statements are TRUE.

questions.text: You are treating your first patient in Surgery Clinic next month.  You are extracting a tooth and remember to use a throat screen as Dr. Wachs mentioned once or twice or many times…However, the throat screen is not completely blocking the pharynx and the tooth slips from your forceps and disappears into the pharynx. Consider the following statements: I. If the patient does not exhibit any symptoms, they should be told what happened and advised to contact their physician or go to an Emergency Room or Urgent Care facility if symptoms develop. II. You should turn the patient to the surgeon with their mouth facing down and ask them not to cough so the tooth does not get into their lungs. III. Chest and/or abdominal radiographs may be able to show if the tooth was aspirated or ingested.
options: Only I and II are TRUE.
Only I and III are TRUE.
Only II and III are TRUE.
I, II, and III are TRUE.
I, II, and III are all NOT TRUE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about alveolar process fractures during extractions is FALSE?
options: Alveolar process fractures are more likely to occur when lone-standing teeth are being extracted.
Alveolar process fractures may occur when excessive force is applied with a forceps due to inadequate prior luxation.
When extracting the most posterior molar tooth in the maxilla, careful separation of the distal bone from the tooth can reduce the chance of a tuberosity fracture occurring.
Alveolar process fracture can result in the creation of an oro-antral communication.
Alveolar process fracture is more common in younger patients versus older patients because bone in younger patients is more elastic.
A bone fragment which results from an alveolar process fracture can be maintained if it remains attached to the soft tissue and has an adequate blood supply.

questions.text: Which of the following characteristics should be considered when assessing the degree of risk of causing an oro-antral communication when a maxillary tooth is being extracted? I. Pneumatization of the alveolus. II. Anatomy of the tooth’s roots III. Relationship of the tooth to the sinus.

Four full-boney impacted third molars were extracted on a young healthy patient.  Swelling increased during post-op days 1 and 2 and steadily decreased over post-op days 3, 4, and 5. However, the patient was barely able to open their mandible by two weeks post-operatively. Consider the following statements: I. Limited opening as described here would be considered normal at 10 days post-op following removal of four full-boney impacted third molars. II. Limited opening as described here is not normal at 14 days post-op following removal of four full-boney impacted third molars and may be due to excess inflammation involving the muscles of mastication due to the surgical procedure itself. III. Limited opening as described here is not normal at 14 days post-op following removal of four full-boney impacted third molars and may be due to excess inflammation involving the muscles of mastication due to the administration of multiple inferior alveolar nerve blocks during the extractions.
options: Only I and II are TRUE.
Only I and III are TRUE.
Only II and III are TRUE.
I, II, and III are TRUE.
I, II, and III are all NOT TRUE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about secondary bleeding or post-op hemorrhage is FALSE?
options: This bleeding is often due to patients not properly following post-op instructions.
Patients who undergo extractions should be instructed that there is no need to bite down on gauze after two hours.
If post-extraction bleeding stops and then starts again, this does not necessarily mean that there is a problem.
If a patient has persistent bleeding after extractions and examination shows a liver clot at the bleeding site, this clot should be removed in order to achieve hemostasis.
If persistent, prolonged post-op bleeding occurs and does not respond to properly applied appropriate interventions, medical evaluation and intervention may be necessary.

questions.text: A 10 year-old boy is being evaluated after suffering facial trauma.  Which of the statements below are FALSE?
options: Neurological, spinal, and airway problems must be ruled-out.
The dental provider can conclude that there are no fractured teeth if there are no tooth fractures seen on radiographs.
The dental provider should evaluate whether the injuries are consistent with the causative mechanism as described.
The dental provider should report suspected child abuse to the appropriate authorities.
The size of BOTH the pulp chamber and PDL as seen on dental radiographs provides valuable information for the diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis of any dental injuries.

questions.text: Consider the following clinical image depicting a patient who got hit in the mouth: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: Based on the visual examination as revealed in this image, the dental provider can conclude that teeth #24 and #25 are lingually displaced because they have been luxated from their sockets.
Based on the visual examination as revealed in this image, the dental provider can conclude that teeth #24 and #25 are lingually displaced because of a dentoalveolar fracture.
The dental provider cannot conclude if the teeth were luxated or involved in a dentoalveolar fracture by visual exam only, they must manipulate the teeth to assess their movement.
Orthodontic treatment should be initiated immediately to reposition the teeth.
The teeth should be manually re-positioned and splinted for 12 weeks.

questions.text: All of the following can influence developmental disturbances to a permanent tooth following trauma to a primary tooth EXCEPT:
options: The age of the patient at the time of the trauma.
The stage of the crown formation of the primary tooth.

questions.text: All of the following are potential negative consequences to permanent teeth following trauma to a primary tooth EXCEPT:

Consider the following statements: I. It is contraindicated to reimplant an avulsed primary incisor. II. An intruded primary incisor which “collided” with and is in contact with the permanent tooth bud should be allowed to spontaneously re-erupt.
options: The first statement is true. The second statement is false.
The first statement is false. The second statement is true.

questions.text: The panoramic radiograph and CBCT images shown here are of a 14 year-old.  Clinical examination reveals that the maxillary second molar on the left, tooth #15, is erupted while the maxillary second molar on the right, tooth #2, is unerupted. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: There is no apparent explanation for why #2 has not erupted.
Tooth #2 was probably intruded in a traumatic incident that the patient and her parents cannot recall.

Tooth #1 is positioned inferiorly and palatally to #2 and has blocked its eruption.  Tooth #1 should be removed to allow eruption of well-developed #2 on its own or with orthodontic intervention if necessary.
Tooth #1 is positioned inferiorly and palatally to #2 and has blocked its eruption.  Well-developed tooth #2 should be removed and hopefully tooth #1 will develop normally and erupt.

Tooth #1 is positioned inferiorly and palatally to #2 and has blocked its eruption.  Teeth #1 and #2 should be extracted since it is very unlikely that tooth #2 will erupt on its own or with orthodontic intervention if #1 is removed.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about descriptive pathology terminology is FALSE?
options: Bullae, nodules, and papules are all elevated lesions.
Plaques and macules are flat, non-elevated lesions.
Hyperplastic lesions have an increased size of cells while hypertrophic lesions have an increased number of cells.
Bullae and vesicles are both fluid-containing lesions.
The terms leukoplakia and dysplasia are not interchangeable.

questions.text: Which of the following characteristics of an oral lesion does NOT raise the suspicion of malignancy?
options: Lesion has been present for more than 2 weeks.
Lesion is totally red or speckled red and white.
Lesion and surrounding tissue are firm to the touch.

questions.text: Consider the following statements: I. Cytology-, vital-stain, light-, and molecular-based adjuncts have eliminated the need for surgical biopsy. II. Cytology-, vital stain-, light-, and molecular-based adjuncts have eliminated the need for conventional visual oral examinations. III. Toluidine blue, which has an affinity for tissue expressing high cellular activity, can be useful during surgical procedures to determine the extent of an oral lesion and help the surgeon determine the borders of the excision.
options: Only I and II are TRUE.
Only I and III are TRUE.
Only II and III are TRUE.
I, II, and III are TRUE.
I, II, and III are all NOT TRUE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding biopsy techniques is TRUE?
options: False positive results  indicating dysplasia may be obtained from an incisional biopsy because of variation within the lesion.
An incisional biopsy specimen should be taken from the center of a suspicious lesion.
If an excisional biopsy is performed, a pathologic diagnosis is not necessary since the lesion is being totally removed.
Incisional biopsy is indicated for lesions less than 1 cm if excision of the entire lesion would be accompanied by significant risk to a vital structure in close proximity to the lesion.
Local anesthesia should be injected directly into a suspicious lesion being biopsied to ensure both adequate pain control and hemostasis.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about marsupialization techniques is TRUE?
options: Marsupialization can be used to allow solid tumors to shrink down to avoid damage to vital structures or teeth in proximity to the tumor if complete excision was otherwise performed.
Immediate reconstruction can be performed at the same time as marsupialization if the lesion is benign.
Immediate reconstruction can be performed at the same time as marsupialization if the lesion is malignant.
Marsupialization can be used to allow cystic lesions to shrink down to avoid damage to vital structures or teeth in proximity to the cyst if complete excision was otherwise performed.
Two of the answer statements given here are TRUE.

questions.text: Which of these statements about various techniques used to manage jaw tumors is TRUE?
options: Marsupialization of jaw tumors is the least aggressive technique that should be utilized for malignant lesions.
When enucleation of jaw tumors is utilized for benign, non-aggressive lesions, peripheral ostectomy should always be performed.
Composite resection involves excision of the lesion with wide margins and may require adjunctive therapies such as radiation and/or chemotherapy.
Marginal or segmental bone resection results in disruption of the continuity of bone.
Partial bone resection causes less functional impairment than marginal or segmental bone resection.

questions.text: Which space infection has the most direct route to extend to the diaphragm?
Which of the statements below related to pericoronitis is TRUE?
options: Most cases of pericoronitis involve bacteria other than normal oral flora.
Pericoronitis does not only occur at wisdom teeth.
This condition can be reliably and permanently cured by removal of the gingiva overlying a partially erupted mandibular third molar.
Operculectomy procedures should be done with extreme caution as they may result in damage to the inferior alveolar nerve.
A 1 mm arcuate zone posterior to an impacted mandibular third molar is indicative of the presence of a cyst.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about CT with contrast is TRUE?
options: If a CT scan with contrast is indicated to evaluate an infection, premedication with IV steroids or IV antihistamine can be considered for a patient with a previous allergy to IV contrast.
If a CT scan with contrast is indicated to evaluate an infection, premedication with an appropriate antibiotic can be considered for a patient with a previous allergy to IV contrast.
Allergy to contrast medium is an absolute contraindication to a CT scan with contrast, even if the infection is extremely severe.
Allergy to iodine is an absolute contraindication to a CT scan with contrast, even if the infection is extremely severe.
CT with contrast is critical for evaluation of a periapical abscess.

questions.text: Consider the following statements: I. Increases in WBC, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, glucose, c-reactive protein, and platelet levels may all be related to the presence of infection. II. Gram stain will immediately identify the exact causative organism of an infection, so that the treating clinician does not need to wait 1 to 5 days for the results of culture and sensitivity to prescribe the most specific antibiotic. III. The only benefit in performing an incision and drainage of an infection is to obtain a sample of the organism(s) causing the infection.
options: Only I and II are TRUE.
Only I and III are TRUE.
Only II and III are TRUE.
I, II, and III are TRUE.
I, II, and III are all NOT TRUE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding incision and drainage procedures is TRUE?
options: Intraoral drainage of the submandibular and submental spaces is ideally performed via an intraoral approach.
There is no benefit to performing an incision and drainage of a cellulitis.
Incision and drainage is most effective when all loculations of pus are broken down.
Resolution of an abscess is of paramount importance, so it is not necessary to consider risks to nerves and blood vessels when performing incision and drainage procedures.
The presence of purulence makes it more difficult to achieve adequate local anesthesia, so the best way to obtain adequate local anesthesia is to inject the anesthetic directly into an abscess.

questions.text: Which of these statements about the mylohyoid muscle is FALSE?
options: It is the superior border of the submental space.
It is the inferior border of the sublingual space.
It divides the submandibular gland into two portions.
It is inferior to the lingual nerve.
It is superior to the submandibular duct.

questions.text: Which of these statements about impacted teeth is TRUE?
options: Impacted teeth will not erupt after the age of 25.
Ectopic eruption of maxillary canines will occur more commonly in a palatal rather than a labial position.
Treatment of impacted teeth should only be initiated if the patient is having symptoms.
Tooth impaction may occur in the area of a cleft palate.
Systemic factors that are associated with impacted teeth will usually only affect a single tooth.

questions.text: Consider the following statements about impacted teeth: I. Pell and Gregory numerical classification of impacted third molars is based on the relationship of the tooth to the anterior border of the ramus. II. Pell and Gregory alphabetical classification of impacted third molars is based on the relationship of the tooth to the occlusal surface of the adjacent second molar. III. Extraction of impacted teeth decreases in difficulty as Pell and Gregory Classification goes from A to C and from 1 to 3.
options: Only I and II are TRUE.
Only I and III are TRUE.
Only II and III are TRUE.
I, II, and III are TRUE.
I, II, and III are all NOT TRUE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the degree of difficulty of extracting impacted teeth is FALSE?
options: Tooth buds with no root formation are more difficult to remove than teeth with 1/3 - 2/3 root formation.
Extraction of fully formed impacted teeth in patients older than 35 generally requires more bone removal than extraction of similar teeth in younger patients.
Distoangular impacted mandibular third molars are easier to extract than mesioangular impacted mandibular third molars because they can be elevated away from the adjacent second molar.
Mesioangular impacted maxillary third molars are more difficult to extract than distoangular maxillary impacted third molars because elevator access and positioning is more difficult.
Both wider PDL space and wider follicular sacs make extractions of impacted third molars easier.

questions.text: Consider the panoramic radiograph of a 13 year-old shown here: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: Both maxillary canines should be extracted because it is extremely unlikely that they will erupt into a healthy position.
The maxillary third molars should be extracted at this time as it is extremely unlikely that they will erupt due to their severe impaction.
The maxillary third molars should be extracted at this time as the lack of root formation makes this a relatively simple procedure.

The maxillary left canine should be extracted because it is extremely unlikely that it will erupt into a healthy position.  However, the maxillary right canine should not be extracted because it will likely erupt into a healthy position.
None of these statements is TRUE.

questions.text: Consider the following two statements about the extraction of impacted mandibular third molars: I. In general, the greater the extent of bone removed during the extraction of an impacted mandibular third molar, the worse the post-operative course will be. B. Minimizing the extent of bone removed during the extraction of an impacted mandibular third molar may not improve the post-operative course if it leads to increased surgical time and force required for the extraction.
options: The first statement is true. The second statement is false.
The first statement is false. The second statement is true.

questions.text: Consider the following statements regarding differences in extraction of impacted maxillary third molars differs compared to extraction of impacted mandibular third molars: I. Removal of bone with a handpiece is rarely necessary for maxillary third molars. II. Sectioning of the tooth is rarely necessary for maxillary third molars. III. A regular handpiece rather than a surgical handpiece can be used for maxillary third molars if bone removal or sectioning is necessary.
options: Only I and II are TRUE.
Only I and III are TRUE.
Only II and III are TRUE.
I, II, and III are TRUE.
I, II, and III are all NOT TRUE.

questions.text: Consider this panoramic radiograph taken on a patient who was referred for extraction of the maxillary right third molar for periodontal considerations. Which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: During the extraction of this tooth, the adjacent bridge may be broken or dislodged.
During extraction of this tooth, the risk of tuberosity fracture may be reduced by careful separation of the distal bone from the tooth with periosteal and/or dental elevators.
This tooth can be safely removed without any additional imaging.
Additional imaging will not provide any benefit for extraction of the mandibular third molars.
The radiolucent lesion at the mandibular left third molar should be submitted for pathologic diagnosis.

questions.text: Consider the following panoramic radiograph taken on a 67 year-old male who had a recent extraction of his mandibular left second molar. Which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: If the impacted mandibular right third molar and supernumerary tooth are extracted, there is a risk that the mandible could fracture at the surgical site intraoperatively.

If the impacted mandibular right third molar and supernumerary tooth are extracted, there is a risk of temporary post-operative neurosensory disturbance that can occur due to damage to the inferior alveolar nerve.

If the impacted mandibular right third molar and supernumerary tooth are extracted, there is a risk of permanent post-operative neurosensory disturbance that can occur due to damage to the inferior alveolar nerve.
There was a risk of fracture of the mandible at the site of the impacted teeth on the mandibular right during the recent extraction of the mandibular left second molar.
There is no legitimate reason to obtain a CBCT if the impacted teeth at the right mandible become symptomatic and require treatment since treatment would be the same no matter what the CBCT shows.

questions.text: Consider the following panoramic radiograph: Extraction of the mandibular left third molar is indicated due to repeated episodes of pericoronitis. Consider the following actions that may be utilized during extraction of this tooth. I. Elevation of a split-thickness mucoperiosteal flap. II. Elevation of a full-thickness mucoperiosteal flap. III. Sectioning of tooth. IV. Use of surgical handpiece to cut a lingual trough. V. Use of surgical handpiece to cut a buccal trough. VI. Removal of tooth segments. VII. Irrigation of site and closure by suturing. Which of the following describes the correct steps in order for extraction of this tooth?
options: II, IV, V, III, VI, VII.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about absorbable sutures is FALSE?
options: They should not be used in deep layers.
They can cause scarring if used externally.
Chromic gut is commonly used intraorally.
They can be helpful in preventing hematoma formation in a deep wound.

questions.text: Consider the following two statements: I. 3-0 and 4-0 sutures are commonly used intraorally. II. 7/0 sutures are larger in diameter than 2/0 sutures.
options: I is true. II is false.
I is false. II is true.

The patient could be taking the warfarin for which of the following medical conditions?
You work with the patient’s physician to implement a strategy to manage his warfarin in the perioperative period. Which of the following strategies makes the most sense?
options: Stop the warfarin for 3 days prior to the procedure.
Check his platelet count.  If it is in the normal range, surgery can be done without adjusting the warfarin.
Adjust his warfarin dosing so that his INR is greater than 4 and then do the surgery.
Do the surgery and if his post-operative bleeding is too heavy or too prolonged, stop the warfarin and resume it after the bleeding stops.
Adjust his warfarin dosing so that his INR is between 2.0 and 2.5 and do the surgery.

questions.text: The patient is extremely anxious and opts to be sedated for the procedure.  Pre-operative sedation instructions include nothing to eat or drink for 8 hours prior to the procedure.  Which of the following strategies should be used to manage the patient’s insulin in the peri-operative period?
options: Have the patient skip their morning insulin.  Check their glucose levels throughout the procedure. If their glucose level drops too low, give them IV dextrose as necessary to prevent hypoglycemia.
Even though normally a patient is supposed to not eat prior to being sedated, this patient should be allowed to eat since they are on insulin.

Have the patient take their usual dose of regular insulin and ½ dose NPH before the procedure.  Check their glucose levels throughout the procedure. If their glucose level drops too low, give them IV dextrose as necessary to prevent hypoglycemia.
Tell the patient to not take any insulin until they are able to eat normally.  When they can eat normally, they can resume their normal insulin dosing.
Have the patient skip their morning insulin.  After the procedure, the patient can call their physician and he/she can manage their insulin.

questions.text: Several considerations figure into the design of the flap and placement of the incisions for this surgical procedure. Which of the following is not a pertinent consideration?
options: The position of the mental nerve.
The position of the mental foramen.
The position of the lingual nerve.
The flap should allow adequate access to remove the lesion.
Retraction of the flap should be able to be accomplished without tearing the flap.

questions.text: Which of the following flap designs could be used for this procedure?
options: Vertical releasing incision made directly over the lesion.
Horizontal incision made directly over the lesion.
Double-Y incision made directly over the lesion.
Envelope flap with a vertical releasing incision at least two teeth anterior to the lesion.
Envelope flap confined to the gingival sulcus of teeth #28 and #29.

questions.text: Once the flap has been reflected, which of the following instruments can be used to remove the lesion from the boney cavity?
Which of the following statements regarding post-surgical pain control for this patient is TRUE?
options: Acetaminophen should not be given to this patient since he is on warfarin.
Acetaminophen with codeine should not be given to this patient since he is on warfarin.
Ibuprofen should not be given to this patient since he is on warfarin.
Narcotics should not be given to this patient since he is on warfarin.
Since this patient is on warfarin, he should not be given any analgesic medications.

questions.text: On post-op Day 1 the patient develops a soft facial swelling in the area overlying the surgical site. This swelling resolves by the end of post-op Day 3. On Post-op Day 6 the patient develops fever and extraoral swelling, tenderness, and erythema of his cheek confined to the area just lateral to tooth #29 and extending approximately 1 cm anterior and posterior to this area.  The swelling feels fluctuant.  It does not extend inferiorly under the patient’s mandible or into his neck.  There is no swelling on the lingual surface of his mandible or in the floor of his mouth. Which of the following statements is most consistent with the findings presented here?
options: The patient has developed a buccal space infection.
The patient has developed a submandibular space infection.
The patient has developed a sublingual space infection.
The patient has developed a submental space infection.
The patient does not have an infection.  This is normal post-operative swelling.

questions.text: You find out that the patient’s hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) is 10.  Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: The patient’s diabetes is poorly controlled so he is more prone to developing an infection than a nondiabetic patient and any infection he develops would be more difficult to control than in a non-diabetic patient.

The patient’s diabetes is well-controlled so he is no more prone to developing an infection than a nondiabetic patient and any infection he develops would not be more difficult to control than in a nondiabetic patient.

The patient’s diabetes is poorly controlled so he is no more prone to developing an infection than a non-diabetic patient but any infection he develops would be more difficult to control than in a nondiabetic patient.

The patient’s diabetes is poorly controlled so he is more prone to developing an infection than a nondiabetic patient but any infection he develops would not be more difficult to control than in a non-diabetic patient.
Hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) values do not provide any information regarding a patient’s diabetes control.

questions.text: You decide that the patient does have an infection so you perform an incision and drainage procedure. Which of the following statements makes the most sense?
options: You obtain pus and conclude that the infection is a cellulitis.
You obtain pus and submit it for culture and sensitivity testing.  You hold off on prescribing antibiotics until you receive the results of this testing.

You obtain pus and submit it for culture and sensitivity testing.  You prescribe the antibiotic that you think will most likely work and will consider changing it based on the patient’s condition and the results of the sensitivity testing.
You obtain pus but do not need to prescribe antibiotics since you feel you removed all of the pus so the infection should resolve.
You do not obtain pus so you decide that you were wrong and the patient does not have an infection so you do not prescribe antibiotics.

questions.text: Everything resolves and the patient has no problems for 7 months.  At that time swelling and symptoms recur.  The patient returns and after a lengthy discussion, you and the patient agree that the best course of action is to extract #29 at this time. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE? I. The extraction forceps can be used to luxate the tooth with buccal and lingual movements. II. The extraction forceps can be used to luxate the tooth with mesial and distal movements. III. This tooth generally come out towards the buccal so the extraction forceps should only be used to luxate the tooth with buccal movements. IV. The extraction forceps can be used to rotate this tooth.
Which of the instruments listed here can generally be used for extraction of tooth #29? I. Ash forceps. II. Rongeur. III. 151 forceps. IV. 150 forceps.
options: I, II, and IV. The following scenario applies to questions 50 – 53: A 12 year-old patient presents to your office three days after suffering a traumatic dental injury. Upon clinical examination you notice that both teeth #8 and #9 are fractured. Tooth #8 has a small pinpoint pulpal exposure while tooth #9 does not. Patient reports severe pain in the upper anterior region which keeps him up at night. Clinical testing: #7 (-) percussion (-) palpation (+) cold, non lingering #8 (-) percussion (-) palpation (+) cold , non lingering. #9 (+) percussion (-) palpation (-) cold #10 (-) percussion (-) palpation (+) cold, non lingering.

questions.text: The treatment of choice for tooth #9 is:
The treatment of choice for tooth #8 is:

Five years after the traumatic incident you notice that tooth #8 has a horizontal fracture in the apical third.  This was picked up on a routine radiographic examination.  You look back at the initial radiographs and realize the fracture was present at that time, although you failed to diagnose it.  The patient is asymptomatic. There are no other radiographic findings. There is no mobility of the tooth.  The best approach at this point would be:
options: Root canal therapy up to the fracture line.
Extraction and replacement with an implant.
Inform the patient about the fracture and eave it alone and monitor.
Leave it alone and don’t tell the patient since you missed diagnosing the fracture previously.

questions.text: BONUS: Since this patient reported a history of having had coronary stents placed, he must have had a myocardial infarction and sustained damage to his heart.

Please refer to the attached pdf for the case scenario. It was decided to delay the extraction until the patient has not taken warfarin for two days. The extraction was performed without re-checking the INR. The patient calls several hours after the extraction and reports that he has heavy bleeding that will not stop. Which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: The patient should be evaluated to see how heavy the bleeding is and if intervention is required.
The INR should be re-checked and if it is not 1.0 or below, it should be assumed that this is the cause of the bleeding.
Local measures such as the application of hemostatic agents and re-suturing can be used to help reduce the bleeding.
Post-operative instructions should be reviewed with the patient to make sure he is doing everything correctly.
The INR should have been re-checked before the extraction was done.

questions.text: Please refer to the attached pdf for the case scenario. Which of the following statements about this patient's post-operative pain management is TRUE?
options: It is safe for him to take acetaminophen.
It is safe for him to take NSAIDS.
It is safe for him to take a combination of acetaminophen and NSAIDS.
He should not take any analgesics until his pain has reached a significant level.
He should expect to be pain-free when following the post-operative pain management protocol.

questions.text: Please refer to the attached pdf for the case scenario. Which of these statements about the mandibular right third molar (#32) is TRUE?
options: The surgeon might as well extract #32 at the same time as #31 since the patient is already having a procedure in that area.
One of the periapical radiographs shows #32 entirely, so no other images would be necessary when deciding when and how to extract that tooth.
After #31 is extracted, #32 may erupt to some degree over time.
#32 must be extracted since it is impacted.
Extracting #32 would be easier now than when the patient was much younger since the surrounding bone is more elastic.

questions.text: Please refer to the attached pdf for the case scenario. Review of the imaging studies reveals the following about tooth #31: - Carious - Periapical pathology - Roots impinging on a narrowed inferior alveolar nerve - Crown an adjacent #30 Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: Extraction of #31 does not pose any risk of neurosensory disturbance since this is a second molar, not a third molar.
Coronectomy is a good option for treatment of this tooth.
If the tooth fractures during extraction, the apical fragment can be left in place.

A throat screen should be used during the extraction since the adjacent tooth has a crown which could be dislodged during the extraction. Otherwise, use of a throat screen would not be necessary when performing the extraction.
NONE of these statements are TRUE.

questions.text: Please refer to the attached pdf for the case scenario. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: This patient's diabetes makes him more prone to developing an infection and if an infection does develop it will be more severe compared to a person without diabetes.
This patient's diabetes does not make him more prone to developing an infection but if an infection does develop, it will be more severe compared to a person without diabetes.
If the patient is having surgery first thing in the morning with sedation and needs to be NPO for eight hours prior to the sedation he should take his insulin as he normally does.
If the patient is having surgery first thing in the morning with sedation and needs to be NPO for eight hours prior to the sedation he should double his insulin doses.
During the peri-operative period, mild to moderate hyperglycemia puts the patient at greater risk than hypoglycemia.

questions.text: Please refer to the attached pdf for the case scenario. Which of the following statements about this patient's anticoagulation status and management is TRUE?
options: There is no risk in administering protamine sulfate which would reverse the effects of the warfarin.
There is no risk in administering Vitamin K which would reverse the effects of the warfarin.
The 4.5 INR is in the target range for preventing blood clot formation.
The general dentist should have decided to take the patient off his warfarin before sending him to the surgeon.
The patient was most likely taking the warfarin to reduce the risk of blood clots and stroke because of his atrial fibrillation.

questions.text: Please refer to the attached pdf for the case scenario. Which of the following statements about this patient's heart rate is FALSE?
options: This patient's heart rate is in the normal heart rate range.
This patient's heart rate (54) is most likely due to the metoprolol, a beta blocker used for his hypertension.
This patient's heart rate (54) is most likely due to the patient being in pain.
This patient's heart rate (54) is most likely due to the patient's dental phobia/anxiety.
This patient's heart rate (54) is most likely due to the patient being a well-trained athlete.

questions.text: Please refer to the attached pdf for the case scenario. What ASA Classification would you assign to this patient?
Consider the sutures depicted in this photograph: Which of these statements regarding the sutures shown here is TRUE?
options: S1 is a continuous “baseball” suture and S2 is a continuous “football” suture.
S1 is a continuous “baseball” suture and S2 is a continuous interlocking suture.
S1 is a continuous interlocking suture and S2 is a continuous “baseball” suture.
S1 is a continuous sling suture and S2 is a continuous “baseball” suture.
S1 is a continuous interlocking suture and S2 is a continuous sling suture.

questions.text: Which of the following statements related to suturing is TRUE?
options: Sutures should be pulled tight to ensure good closure of a wound or incision.
No matter how deep a wound or incision is, it is only necessary to close the tissue at the surface.
Using a curved needle makes suturing more difficult.
A 10-0 size suture has a larger diameter than a 3-0 size suture.
Sutures should be placed at equal depths and distances on both sides of a wound or incision.

questions.text: Which of the following signs or techniques should NOT be used to diagnose an oro-antral communication following an extraction?
options: Examine the tooth for bone attached to the roots.
Observe for drainage from the socket.
Listen for air movement through the socket.
Pinch the patient's nostrils closed and observe for blood bubbles in the socket.
None of these - all of these signs or techniques should be used to diagnose an oro-antral communication following an extraction.

questions.text: Which of the following techniques and/or circumstances DECREASES the risk or likelihood of causing TMJ injuries when performing mandibular extractions?
options: Application of excessive forces during the extraction
Having the patient bite down on a bite block while the operator or an assistant pushes up on the anterior inferior border of the mandible.
Using a 3-corner flap rather than an envelope flap.

questions.text: A tooth may accidentally be displaced into the infratemporal fossa during extraction of a maxillary third molar. Which of the following statements regarding treatment is FALSE?
options: If the tooth is visible at the time of displacement, it should be grasped and removed.
If the tooth is not visible at the time of displacement, no more than five blind attempts should be made to grasp it and remove it.

If the tooth cannot be immediately removed at the time of displacement, the site should be sutured, antibiotics should be prescribed, and the patient should be informed of the need for future removal of the tooth.
If the tooth cannot be immediately removed at the time of displacement, removal should be delayed, allowing fibrosis to occur and stabilize the tooth, avoiding further displacement.
Delayed removal of the displaced tooth is generally beyond the scope and capabilities of a general dentist and should be referred to an Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about post-operative hemorrhage following an extraction is FALSE?
options: It often occurs due to a patient's failure to properly follow instructions.
It may occur due to a “liver clot” which is a blood clot that forms outside of the extraction socket.
Injecting local anesthesia with epinephrine into the surgical site may help achieve hemostasis but it may also mask bleeding which could resume when the epinephrine effects wear off.
It is always related to local factors and not a result of systemic medical issues or medications that the patient may be taking.
Biting on a teabag may help slow or stop bleeding.

questions.text: Which of the following instructions are NOT included in “sinus precautions” given to a patient when a maxillary posterior extraction may have resulted in an oro-antral communication?
options: Do not blow your nose for two weeks.
Do not do any heavy lifting.
All of these instructions are included in “sinus precautions”.

questions.text: Which of the following statements relating to maintaining hemostasis following oral surgical procedures is a TRUE statement that should be included in the instructions given to the patient?
options: The purpose of the patient biting on gauze after a procedure is to soak up the blood coming from the surgical site.
Bleeding can start and stop after a procedure and often is heavier after the numbing wears off.
It is extremely unusual for some bleeding to persist throughout the first 24 hours
The longer the blood clot is kept in the extraction site, the greater the likelihood of developing a painful condition known as a DRY SOCKET.
Patients can rinse, spit, smoke, use a straw, or do heavy lifting beginning one hour after an extraction.

questions.text: Which of the following techniques is NOT a primary treatment modality for jaw tumors?
options: All of these techniques can be primary treatment modalities for jaw tumors.
None of these techniques can be primary treatment modalities for jaw tumors.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about reconstruction following resection of jaw tumors is FALSE?
options: Delayed reconstruction is recommended when the patient has both intraoral and extraoral defects.
A disadvantage of immediate reconstruction is the potential for recurrence which may necessitate further surgery.
If reconstruction is delayed, it is not necessary to maintain the proper anatomical position of mandibular segments.
A disadvantage of immediate reconstruction is the potential for loss of the graft due to infection.
Maintaining the inferior border of the mandible, if possible, aids in reconstruction.

questions.text: Consider this image depicting a portion of the mandible removed during a resection: Which of the following best describes the type of resection which was performed?
Which of the following statements about marsupialization is TRUE?
options: The portion of the lesion which is not removed during a marsupialization procedure cannot be diagnosed and may contain a more aggressive lesion than the tissue which is removed.
Marsupialization inconveniences patients as they are required to irrigate the site once per week.
Tissue cannot be obtained for pathologic diagnosis when marsupialization is performed.
Marsupialization is a definitive treatment after which no additional treatment is necessary.
The risk of mandible fracture related to a large mandibular lesion is reduced immediately following the marsupialization procedure.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about marsupialization is FALSE?
options: This technique may be helpful to avoid neurovascular injury when a cystic lesion is in close proximity to the inferior alveolar nerve.
This technique may be helpful to avoid an oro-antral fistula when removing a solid tumor of the posterior maxilla.
This technique may be helpful to allow eruption of a tooth that has been displaced by a cystic lesion.
This technique may allow for a lesser surgery to be utilized when removing some lesions in medically compromised patients.
This lesion may be helpful to lessen the risk of fracture when removing a large cyst of the posterior mandible.

questions.text: Which of the following statements related to biopsy procedures is FALSE?
options: Suction can cause increased bleeding during biopsy procedures.
The specimen can accidentally be lost via suctioning.
Suction can cause tissue damage during biopsy procedures.
If palpation reveals that a lesion is pulsatile, aspiration prior to biopsy is not necessary.
Blotting, compression, clamping, silver nitrate, cautery, and laser can all be useful for achieving hemostasis during biopsy procedures.

questions.text: If a symmetric canine bulge does not exist in a patient's vestibule by age 6, then radiographic assessment &/or orthodontic consultation is indicated.
A maxillary impacted canine is to be exposed so that it can be erupted orthodontically. The technique should be selected to ensure all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Adequate attached gingiva surrounding the tooth.
Healthy periodontal status of the adjacent teeth.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding coronectomy procedures is TRUE?
options: A panoramic radiograph is the only imaging modality needed to decide between extraction and coronectomy of a mandibular their molar.
There is no risk of damaging the inferior alveolar nerve during coronectomy of a mandibular third molar.
The root fragment left in place during coronectomy of a mandibular third molar may need to be extracted in the future.
There are no contraindications to coronectomy procedures.
The tooth fragment that is left in place during a coronectomy should be cut even with the bone margin at the surgical site.

questions.text: Which of the following steps after removal of an impacted tooth is INCORRECT?
options: Any areas of sharp bone should be smoothed.
Follicular fragments or pathology should be removed.
The socket and area under the flap should be irrigated to remove any tooth and/or bone debris.
The surgical site should be checked for adequate hemostasis.
Soft tissues surrounding the extraction site should be sutured tightly over the socket to achieve primary closure.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about flap design and development for the removal of impacted third molars is TRUE?
options: The general principles for designing and developing a flap are different for erupted teeth and impacted teeth.
When designing and developing a flap to extract a mandibular third molar, the surgeon should remember that the mandible often diverges lingually in this region.
A flap designed for the extraction of a mandibular third molar can de described as a “baseball bat” because of the shape of the flap.
A 3-corner flap with a vertical release is preferred over an envelope flap for the extraction of mandibular third molars because it heals better and is quicker to suture.
A releasing incision can be made at the mesial aspect of second molar to gain increased access when extracting a maxillary third molar that is impacted in a high position.

questions.text: Which of the following statements pertaining to the removal of impacted teeth is TRUE?
options: Post-operative recovery is generally the same following extraction of impacted teeth as the recovery following extraction of erupted teeth.
Longer surgeries result in decreased swelling and shorter healing periods than shorter surgeries.
When sectioning an impacted tooth, it is necessary to drill through the entire tooth from the buccal to the lingual.
A skilled surgeon should be able to extract an impacted tooth with either bone removal or sectioning, but should not need to do both on the same tooth.
Insufficient bone removal and/or sectioning may complicate an extraction as the use of increased force may then become necessary.

questions.text: It is important to assess the potential for damage to the inferior alveolar canal during extraction of a mandibular third molar. Which of the following findings on panoramic radiographs is NOT indicative of the position of a mandibular third molar relative to the inferior alveolar nerve?
options: Interruption of the superior cortical border of the inferior alveolar nerve canal by a portion of the tooth.
Deflection of the inferior alveolar canal at the tooth.
Narrowing of the inferior alveolar canal at the tooth.
Darkening of the root of the tooth where the inferior alveolar nerve overlies it on the radiograph.
Extreme anterior positioning of the mental foramen.

questions.text: Options for the management of impacted teeth include any of the following treatments, EXCEPT:
options: Clinical and radiographic observation over time
None of the above - all of these choices are potential options for the management of impacted teeth.

questions.text: Which of the following statements related to maxillary tuberosity fracture during an extraction is FALSE?
options: Tuberosity fracture may result in an oro-antral communication.
Tuberosity fracture is more likely to occur with mesioangular impacted maxillary third molars than with distoangular impacted maxillary third molars.
Tuberosity fracture is more likely to occur with increased pneumatization of the tuberosity.
Tuberosity fracture may only occur with extraction of a maxillary third molar - not with any other maxillary teeth.
The risk of causing a tuberosity fracture during extraction of a maxillary third molar can be lessened by careful separation of the distal bone from the tooth with a periosteal or dental elevator.

questions.text: The degree of difficulty of extracting an impacted mandibular third molar is NOT related to:
options: The position of the tooth relative to the anterior border of the ramus.
The position of the tooth relative to the occlusal height of the adjacent second molar.
The proximity of the tooth to the adjacent second molar.
The degree of root development of the tooth.
None of the above - all of these choices influence the degree of difficulty of extracting an impacted mandibular third molar.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding impacted teeth is FALSE?
options: If a mandibular third molar tooth bud begins development in a horizontal position, it will never be able to erupt.
The amount of space between the mandibular second molar and the ramus can play a role in whether or not the third molar tooth will become impacted.

Decreased flexibility/Increased rigidity of bone contributes to increased treatment complications and more difficult and slower recovery in patients undergoing extraction of impacted teeth at increased age.
Maxillary canines may become impacted because they erupt after the lateral incisor and first premolar and thus have inadequate space.
Local factors that may allow eruption of impacted teeth in older patients include extraction of adjacent teeth and use of a denture overlying the impacted tooth.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a systemic factor associated with tooth impaction?
Late complications following dental trauma can occur up to:
options: 1 month after the trauma has occurred.
6 months after the trauma has occurred.
1 year after the trauma has occurred.
5 years after the trauma has occurred.
10 years after the trauma has occurred

questions.text: On routine exam a patient is found to have a horizontal root fracture in the middle third of #9. It is asymptomatic and not tender on percussion or palpation. There is no mobility. Pulp testing is inconclusive. The patient recalls a history of trauma about 10 years ago. The treatment of choice is:

Which of these statements regarding the reimplantation of primary teeth after avulsion is TRUE?
options: Semi-rigid splinting for 2 - 3 weeks is necessary.
Semi-rigid splinting for 6 weeks is necessary.
Rigid splinting for 2 - 3 weeks is necessary.
Rigid splinting for 6 weeks is necessary.
Primary teeth should not be reimplanted after avulsion.

questions.text: Consider the following diagnoses: I. Complicated crown fracture (open apex) II. Complicated crown fracture (closed apex) III. Root fracture - apical or middle third IV. Extrusion V. Avulsion VI. Alveolar fracture Which of the following choices include injuries that all require a SEMI-RIGID splint?
Which of the following effects on the succedaneous permanent tooth can result from trauma to a primary tooth?
options: White or yellow/brown discoloration and/or hypoplasia of the enamel
Lateral root formation, dilaceration of the root, and/or partial or incomplete root formation
Sequestration of the permanent tooth germ
All of these effects on the succedaneous permanent tooth can result from trauma to a primary tooth.

questions.text: Which of the following factors is not a consideration when assessing the likelihood of success when re-implanting an avulsed tooth?
options: Pre-existing periodontal status of the tooth
Length of time tooth was out of the socket
Degree of root formation/apical closure of the tooth
How the tooth was handled and stored when out of the socket

questions.text: All of the following may be clinical signs of advanced infection, EXCEPT:
options: None of the above - all of these choices may be clinical signs of advanced infection.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about a periapical abscess is TRUE?
options: The location of the swelling provides no useful information when determining the source or cause of the infection.

Trephination - going through the cortical bone to enter the boney abscess cavity - will not resolve the pain caused by a periapical abscess; only definitive treatment such as extraction, endodontic treatment, or apicoectomy can resolve the pain.
A chronic periapical abscess may not be painful if the infection is able to drain via a fistula.
All maxillary anterior teeth with periapical infections will naturally drain on the buccal.

There is no downside to doing an apicoectomy on an endodontically treated tooth with a periapical abscess, other than the possibility that the procedure may not work and the patient may then need the tooth extracted.

questions.text: A patient presents for emergency evaluation of increasing pain of their lower left 3rd molar and swelling of the face. Exam reveals a raised floor of the mouth, as well as non-fluctuant swelling along the left inferior border of the mandible, that is warm and erythematous. The operculum over tooth #17 is edematous and erythematous. A panoramic radiograph reveals a partially impacted tooth #17 with pericoronal radiolucency. You determine that the patient has a cellulitis of odontogenic origin. The infection has likely spread to which space(s)?
The sublingual and submandibular spaces are separated by which muscle?
Which of the following statements regarding treatment of oral infections is TRUE?
options: If a drainage procedure is performed on a true cellulitis, purulence (pus) will be obtained.
If a drainage procedure is performed on a cellulitis, progression to an abscess may be prevented as the procedure can allow oxygen into the site and prevent a shift to anaerobic bacteria.
The technique used for draining an abscess associated with a mandibular first bicuspid is not of critical importance as there is little risk associated with making an incision in this region.
Drainage procedures are most effective when incisions are placed to draw purulence (pus) in an upwards direction against gravity.
Blunt instruments are not effective when dissecting through tissues to perform a drainage procedure.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about PERICORONITIS related to a mandibular third molar is FALSE?
options: Extraction is the most effective treatment for attaining resolution of the infection.
Chlorhexidine and antibiotics may be helpful to attain resolution of the infection.
Local anesthesia may have a diminished effect in the area of pericoronitis.

Operculectomy generally provides long-term resolution of the infection and makes extraction unnecessary. Operculectomy should be accomplished via incision of tissue at the lingual position on the retromolar pad.

Elimination of trauma to the retromolar pad may be helpful in attaining resolution of the acute infection and can be accomplished via extraction of the opposing third molar or reduction of the cusp(s) causing the trauma.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about complications related to impacted teeth is FALSE?
options: Post-operative complications are more common and recovery is more difficult with increased patient age.
Medically compromising conditions can result in impaired post-operative healing.
As patients progress through adolescence to adulthood, increased root development may result in increased risk to vital structures with surgical treatment.
As patients progress through adolescence to adulthood, increased crown development and tooth movement may result in increased risk to adjacent teeth with and without surgical treatment.
Healing/recovery from a nerve injury is not affected by patient age.

questions.text: A patient presents with severe pericoronitis at the site of a horizontally impacted #32 with full root development. #1 is supererupted and is traumatizing the site. The OMFS wants to allow resolution of the infection prior to extraction. Which of the following actions are NOT acceptable treatments that may be helpful in gaining resolution of the pericoronitis?
options: Reducing the offending cusp(s) of #1 with a handpiece.
Irrigating the #32 site with hydrogen peroxide.
ALL of the actions listed here are acceptable treatments that may be helpful in gaining resolution of the pericoronitis.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the classification of impacted teeth is FALSE?
options: The Pell and Gregory Classification System that assigns a numerical value to a tooth is based on the tooth's horizontal position relative to the anterior border of the mandibular ramus.
The Pell and Gregory Classification System that assigns an alphabetical value to a tooth is based on the tooth's vertical position relative to the adjacent second molar.
“Transverse impaction” describes a tooth that is positioned with its occlusal surface pointing to either the buccal or the lingual.
Difficulty of extraction increases with progression through both Pell and Gregory numerical and alphabetical classification systems.
Classifying a tooth based on its overlying tissue is helpful because these classifications correlate directly with the degree of difficulty of extracting that tooth.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the influence of root morphology of impacted teeth on extraction difficulty and risk is FALSE?
options: Impacted teeth with roots that are 1/2 to fully formed are at an optimal stage for extraction.
Impacted teeth with fused conical roots are generally easier to extract compared to similarly positioned teeth with dilacerated roots.
Impacted teeth with roots whose curves follow the path of elevation are easier to extract than impacted teeth with roots whose curves oppose the path of elevation.

Impacted teeth whose root width is wider than the cervical width of the tooth are more difficult to extract compared to impacted teeth whose root width is narrower than the cervical width of the tooth.
Impacted teeth with wider PDL spaces are easier to extract than impacted teeth with narrower PDL spaces.

questions.text: Which of the following findings on a panoramic radiograph is NOT a prognostic indicator of inferior alveolar nerve injury following mandibular third molar extraction?
options: Interruption of superior cortical border of inferior alveolar nerve canal in area of third molar.
Deflection of inferior alveolar nerve canal in area of third molar.
Narrowing of inferior alveolar nerve canal in area of third molar.
Darkening of root of third molar where it crosses the inferior alveolar nerve canal.
Pericoronal radiolucency that is 2 cm or more in diameter and extends superiorly from the CEJ of a third molar whose root apices are superior to the inferior alveolar canal.

questions.text: The maxillary third molar frequently forms the distal wall of the maxillary sinus. Which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: Extraction of a tooth in this position has an increased risk of an oro-antral communication following its extraction.
Extraction of a tooth in this position is more difficult than extraction of a similarly shaped and angulated tooth that is not forming the distal wall of the maxillary sinus.
The surgeon's pre-operative informed consent discussion should emphasize the risks pertinent to this tooth.
A general practitioner who is a competent at performing extractions may consider referring this tooth to an OMFS.
Appropriate pre-operative radiographs will be helpful in assessing risks related to extraction of this tooth.

questions.text: Consider the following statements: Statement 1: When removing impacted teeth, the surgeon should always remove the smallest amount of bone possible to accomplish the extraction. Statement 2: Increased bone removal during the extraction of impacted teeth can weaken the jaw.
options: I and II are both TRUE.
I is TRUE and II is FALSE.
I is FALSE and II is TRUE.
I and II are both FALSE.

questions.text: When designing and creating a flap for the extraction of an impacted mandibular third molar, the surgeon should keep in mind all that all of the following are TRUE, EXCEPT:
options: It takes longer to suture when a vertical release is used.
An envelope flap generally heals better than a flap with a vertical release.
An envelope flap will not allow as much access to the apical portion of the surgical site as a flap with a properly created vertical release.
A larger flap will directly result in more swelling than a smaller flap.
If a vertical release is used, it should begin at the mesial line angle of the second molar and be angled posteriorly and inferiorly.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: A handpiece is rarely needed for bone removal for extraction of an impacted maxillary third molar.
When sectioning an impacted mandibular third molar for removal, the handpiece should be used to cut completely through the crown from buccal to lingual.
The angulation of the tooth should be considered when determining how an impacted tooth should be sectioned for removal.
The curvature of the roots should be considered when determining how an impacted tooth should be sectioned for removal.
Impacted maxillary third molars rarely need to be sectioned for extraction.

questions.text: In general, which of the following statements regarding the extraction of impacted mandibular third molars is TRUE?
options: Vertical impactions are the easiest to extract.
Mesioangular impactions are the easiest to extract.
Horizontal impactions are the easiest to extract.
Distoangular impactions are the easiest to extract.
You cannot make generalizations about how the position of an impacted mandibular third molar will influence the difficulty of its extraction.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding coronectomy of mandibular third molars is TRUE?
options: Inferior alveolar nerve injury cannot occur if a coronectomy is performed.
If all guidelines are adhered to when performing a coronectomy, the remaining root stump will not move or require future removal.
Periapical infection of a tooth in close proximity to the inferior alveolar nerve is an indication for coronectomy rather than extraction.
When CBCT shows that a mandibular third molar is in close proximity to the inferior alveolar and/or lingual nerves, coronectomy may be indicated to avoid injuring these nerves.
When performing a coronectomy, the remaining root fragment should be at least 4 mm from bone margins in all directions.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding exposure of impacted maxillary canines is TRUE?
options: When exposing an impacted maxillary canine to allow passive eruption, the tooth should be approached from the palate.
When exposing an impacted maxillary canine so that the orthodontist can actively effect eruption of that tooth, the tooth should be approached from the palate.
When exposing an impacted maxillary canine to allow passive eruption, the tooth should be approached from the labial.
When exposing an impacted maxillary canine so that the orthodontist can actively effect eruption of that tooth, the tooth should be approached from the labial.

When exposing an impacted maxillary canine to allow passive eruption or to enable the orthodontist to actively effect eruption of that tooth, surgical approach will depend on the position of the tooth.

questions.text: Potential negative sequela to the permanent dentition following trauma to primary teeth include all of the following, EXCEPT:
options: White or yellow/brown discoloration or hypoplasia of the crown
Effects on the root including dilaceration and partial or incomplete formation

questions.text: If a primary tooth is intruded due to trauma
options: It can be observed as it may spontaneously re-erupt.
It can be extracted if it has been significantly displaced.
It may cause problems for the corresponding succedaneous tooth.
It should be accessed for pulpal therapy and orthodontically brought into the dental arch.
The patient should be assessed for other facial or head injuries.

questions.text: A patient presents with an avulsed tooth in the anterior maxilla. Several years ago they avulsed a tooth in the anterior mandible. Which of the following questions is NOT pertinent when determining the treatment and prognosis for this latest avulsed tooth?
options: Is it a permanent or primary tooth?
Does the tooth have an open or closed apex?
What is the pre-existing periodontal condition of the tooth and surrounding dentition?
How long has the tooth been out of its socket?
How has the tooth been handled since the avulsion?
How did the previously avulsed tooth respond to treatment?

questions.text: A tooth cannot develop pulpal necrosis after trauma without fracture and pulpal exposure.
A permanent tooth sustains a horizontal root fracture. The coronal segment is repositioned and splinted. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: Root canal treatment of the coronal tooth segment to the fracture line should be performed as soon as possible.
Root canal treatment of the coronal and apical tooth segments should be performed as soon as possible.
The tooth should be monitored and if pulp necrosis or irreversible pulpitis develops, root canal treatment of the coronal tooth segment to the fracture line should be performed.
The tooth should be monitored and if pulp necrosis or irreversible pulpitis develops, root canal treatment of the coronal and apical segments should be performed.
Root canal will not be necessary if the repositioning and stabilization were completed within one hour of the injury.

questions.text: A patient presents after a blow to their chin causing their upper and lower teeth to hit each other. It is important for the examining dentist to direct extra attention to the __________ teeth.
options: Attention does not need to be given to any of the teeth as they were not traumatized directly.

questions.text: Which of the following groups of definitions is CORRECT?
options: Hyperkeratosis - overgrowth of cornified layer of epithelium Hyperplasia - an increased number of normal cells Hypertrophy - an increase in the size of cells
Hyperkeratosis - overgrowth of cornified layer of epithelium Hyperplasia - an increase in the size of cells Hypertrophy - an increased number of normal cells
Hyperkeratosis - an increased number of normal cells Hyperplasia - overgrowth of cornified layer of epithelium Hypertrophy - an increase in the size of cells
Hyperkeratosis - an increase in the size of cells Hyperplasia - overgrowth of cornified layer of epithelium Hypertrophy - an increased number of normal cells

questions.text: Which of the following information would NOT be considered in determining a differential diagnosis?
options: Systemic diseases the patient may have
Findings on visual examination of lesion
ALL of this information should be considered in determining a differential diagnosis.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about reconstruction following treatment of jaw lesions is FALSE?
options: Delayed reconstruction should be considered if both intraoral and extraoral defects exist at the time of surgery.
If reconstruction is delayed, there is no advantage to maintaining the mandibular segments in proper anatomical position.
Disadvantages of immediate reconstruction include risk of recurrence and loss of graft due to infection.

If the alveolar crest and soft tissue is not involved and excision of the lesion can wait, teeth can be extracted 6 - 8 weeks prior to extraoral lesion excision and reconstruction to avoid having both intraoral and extraoral defects at the same time.
Multiple methods can be used to maintain the mandibular segments in proper anatomical position including MMF (maxillomandibular fixation), external fixation, internal fixation, and splints.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding biopsy techniques is INCORRECT?
options: A general dentist can perform a biopsy.
The surgeon should avoid injecting local anesthesia directly into the lesion.
Suctioning has the potential to cause more bleeding.
When performing an excisional biopsy, a perimeter of normal tissue should be excised in all direction; generally 2 - 3 mm with an additional 2 - 3 mm if malignancy is suspected.
Incisions should be made perpendicular to nerves, blood vessels, and lines of muscular tension whenever possible.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the treatment of solid hard tissue lesions is TRUE?
options: Marsupialization should be used for benign solid tissue lesions only.
Precautionary aspiration prior to surgical entry of a radiolucent lesion is not necessary if the patient does not have a coagulopathy or is not anticoagulated.
If a lesion resists removal, 1 mm of adjacent bone can be removed.
Hard tissue lesions can be approached via either a split thickness or full thickness flap, depending on the specifics of the lesion and the surgeon's preference.
A handpiece should not be used to gain access to a hard tissue lesion as it may damage the tissue being removed.

questions.text: Which of the following factors should be considered when determining the management of jaw tumors?
options: Size and rate of growth of the tumor.
Whether or not reconstruction is anticipated.
ALL of these factors should be considered when determining the management of jaw tumors.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about soft tissue injuries is FALSE?
options: Skin that was abraded or cut should be protected from sun exposure for an extended healing period.
The depth of a soft tissue injury will affect the rate of healing but the length of a soft tissue injury will not affect the rate of healing.
Puncture wounds may become infected due to the introduction of bacteria to deep tissues through a small opening.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the management of displaced teeth or roots is TRUE?
options: If a root fragment is visible in the sinus just above the apex of the socket, judicious bone removal should be performed to allow retrieval of the fragment.
The mesiobuccal root of the maxillary first molar is the root that is most commonly displaced into the maxillary antrum.
If a maxillary third molar is displaced into the infratemporal sinus and it is not easily retrievable, it should be left in place and removed in the future after fibrosis occurs.
If a root of a mandibular third molar is displaced into the floor of the mouth, a lingual split thickness flap should be developed to gain access to retrieve it.
CBCT examination is not useful in assessing the risk of displacing a root of a mandibular third molar into the floor of the mouth.

questions.text: Which of the following actions should be taken if a tooth or other object disappears into the pharynx?
options: The patient's head should be turned toward the surgeon with their mouth positioned downward to allow the object to move away from the pharynx.
The patient's head should be turned toward the surgeon with their mouth positioned upward to allow visualization of the object so that it may be removed.
If the object cannot be accounted for, the Heimlich maneuver should be performed in case the object has entered the lung.
If the object cannot be accounted for, the surgeon should reach into the pharynx as far as they can to see if they can feel and retrieve the object.
If the object cannot be accounted for, bronchoscopy should be performed immediately in case the object has entered the lung.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about inadvertent alveolar bone fracture during tooth extraction is TRUE?
options: There is an increased risk for this complication in younger patients because their bone is less mature and inherently weaker than bone in older patients.
A defect in the alveolus will result whenever an alveolar fracture occurs as the bone fragment will not remain viable and will subsequently be lost.
Maxillary molars with widespread roots should not be luxated with an elevator but should instead be extracted with forceps only to reduce the likelihood of alveolar bone fracture.
Application of an elevator between a maxillary third molar and the bone of the tuberosity can reduce the likelihood of causing a tuberosity fracture during extraction.
A common site for alveolar bone fracture during extraction is the lingual plate at mandibular incisors.

questions.text: Consider the following actions. I. Examining an extracted maxillary molar for the presence of bone attached to the tooth between the roots. II. Having the patient blow their nose and seeing if blood bubbles are present in the extraction site. III. Probing the socket to see how far in the probe can be placed. IV. Listening for air movement through the socket as the patient breathes normally. Which of these techniques is a safe and potentially useful method to help determine if an oro-antral communication occurred during an extraction?
Which of the following statements about flap repair of an oro-antral communication is TRUE?
options: Flap repair of an oro-antral communication is easier when teeth adjacent to the opening are present as these teeth can help support the flap.
Flap repair of an oro-antral communication should be designed so that the suture line is directly over the sinus opening to ensure that predictable closure is achieved.
When performing flap repair of an oro-antral communication, mucosal surfaces should be de-epithelialized as needed so that raw bleeding surfaces can be sutured to one another.
Success of flap repair of an oro-antral communication is not affected by whether or not the sinus is infected.
Repair of an oro-antral communication by buccal flap advancement results in a ridge suface that better resembles normal crestal tissue than when a palatal flap is advanced.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about oral infections is FALSE?
options: The inoculation stage occurs over 0-3 days during which time pus is not present.
The cellulitis stage occurs over 1-5 days and is diagnosed by the presence of pus.
Abscess occurs over 4-7 days with the continued presence of pus.
Rupture follows the path of least resistance.
The microbiology of oral infections has evolved over time.

questions.text: Which of the following choices does not accurately describe a sign or symptom of an airway related issue during a physical evaluation?
options: Difficulty swallowing associated with pharyngeal swelling.
Difficulty sleeping in a supine position.
Patient in a “Sniffing position” associated with a retropharyngeal space infection.
Uvula deviated to the same side as a lateral pharyngeal space infection.
Distant quality to voice associated with a retropharyngeal or lateral pharyngeal infection.
Elevated tongue associated with a floor of the mouth or sublingual space infection.

questions.text: Submental space infections can generally arise from which of the following teeth? I. Maxillary anteriors II. Mandibular anteriors III. Maxillary posteriors IV. Mandibular posteriors
Trismus will be prominent with infection of which of the following spaces?
options: Anterior lateral pharyngeal and masseteric and pterygoid.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about Ludwig's Angina is FALSE?
options: It involves the submandibular spaces bilaterally and submental space in midline
It involves a rapid spread to the lateral pharyngeal and retropharyngeal spaces.
Rapid obstruction of the upper airway occurs.
The patient may exhibit mouth pain, stiff neck, drooling, and dysphagia.
The retruded tongue position which is evident on clinical examination can cause respiratory difficulty by obstructing the airway.

questions.text: Which of the following processes/signs/symptoms is consistent with Cavernous Sinus Thrombosis?
options: Anterior route of spread via the facial vein.
Posterior route of spread via the angular vein.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about suturing is FALSE?
options: Sutures should be placed at equal internal and external distances from the wound margins.
Sutures should be placed as tightly as necessary to maintain wound closure.
Wound edges should be everted, especially when suturing skin.
Wounds tend to contract when healing.

questions.text: Consider these 4 images in the attachment.
options: Images I and II depict a hemostat and its beaks.
Images I and IV depict a hemostat and its beaks.
Images II and III depict a hemostat and its beaks.
Images III and IV depict a hemostat and its beaks.
Images I, II, III, and IV depict two different types of hemostats.

questions.text: The following scenario and radiograph applies to these questions. A 51 year-old female presented to her general dentist complaining of severe pain at tooth #32. She reported that she was having difficulty eating and she was just consuming liquids. She also reported that she was constantly thirsty, urinating frequently, and tired. She reported a history of Type II diabetes for which she was prescribed metformin. She has not taken the Metformin for the past 2 months because she reported that she was not feeling well while taking it. She last saw her physician 3 months ago and they are unaware that she stopped her medication. Clinical examination revealed a partially exposed #32 with swollen pericoronal gingiva, extending along the lingual margin of 31.  She had mild swelling and tenderness along the right mandibular angle, She was able to open her mouth to a maximum interincisal distance of 30 mm. Panoramic radiograph is shown here: Which of the following questions is the LEAST USEFUL for helping her dentist to assess the serious acute risk that this patient might be facing and determine how they will treat the patient?
options: Is the patient having difficulty eating because her tooth is bothering her or she is having problems swallowing?
Has she checked her blood glucose today?
Does she have any other medical problems?
Is she on any other medications?

questions.text: The following scenario and radiograph applies to these questions. A 51 year-old female presented to her general dentist complaining of severe pain at tooth #32. options: Full thickness flap, buccal trough/bone removal, sectioning of tooth, elevation/removal of fragments, irrigation of socket, suturing.
Full thickness flap, sectioning of tooth, buccal trough/bone removal, elevation/removal of fragments, irrigation of socket, suturing.
