questions.text: The following scenario applies to these questions. A patient has multiple medical problems. He was treated with steroids for asthma for one week one year ago. He is on warfarin for atrial fibrillation. He requires extraction of #14. You call the patient's physician to discuss treatment. The physician immediately tells you the patient is “cleared for treatment” and you can proceed with the extraction.
options: You should proceed with treatment since the patient is cleared.
You should seek the opinion of another physician.
You should check the physician's online reviews to decide if you should accept the physician's clearance.
You should discuss the patient's condition and treatment with the physician and decide what you are doing after consulting with the physician.

questions.text: The following scenario applies to these questions. A patient has multiple medical problems. He was treated with steroids for asthma for one week one year ago. He is on warfarin for atrial fibrillation. He requires extraction of #14. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?
options: This extraction should be performed in the hospital since the patient was on steroids.
This patient requires steroid supplementation because they may not be able to respond to the stress of the surgery.
In general, an adrenally suppressed patient can undergo tooth extraction without steroid supplementation.
The amount of steroids that this patient received would cause adrenal suppression.

questions.text: The following scenario applies to these questions. A patient has multiple medical problems. He was treated with steroids for asthma for one week one year ago. He is on warfarin for atrial fibrillation. He requires extraction of #14. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?
options: Prior to extraction, the warfarin should be discontinued for 3 days.
Prior to extraction, it is not necessary to discontinue the warfarin.
Prior to extraction, the warfarin should be discontinued for 10 days.
Prior to extraction, the patient's INR should be obtained to determine how to manage the warfarin.
Prior to extraction, the patient's platelet count should be obtained to determine how to manage the warfarin.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: If the patient's physician insists that the patient's anticoagulation is interrupted for as short a time as possible, a shorter acting anticoagulant can be used in the peri-operative period to minimize the interruption.
If the patient was on Direct Acting Oral Anticoagulants instead of warfarin, their INR would be critical for determining peri-operative management.
If you could not reach the patient’s physician, you should do the extraction and stop the warfarin because you cannot take a chance of causing a bleeding problem.
If you could not reach the patient’s physician, you should do the extraction and not stop the warfarin for the extraction because you cannot take a chance of causing the patient to have a stroke.

If the patient is in pain post-operatively, their blood pressure will increase and they will have more bleeding. The patient should be advised to take ibuprofen post-operatively so that they are not in pain and will be at lower risk of bleeding.

questions.text: Which of the following is the BEST description of a valid informed consent for a medical or surgical procedure?
options: A note in the medical record which is signed by the treating doctor, the patient, and a witness, in which the patient gives the doctor permission to treat them.

A witnessed discussion between the treating doctor and the patient in which the proposed treatment is discussed. The discussion should include a description of the procedure, the risks and benefits of the procedure, the likelihood of success of the procedure, and any alternatives to the treatment and the risks and benefits of those alternatives
A witnessed discussion between the treating doctor and the patient in which it is made clear that treatment must be provided - doing nothing is not an option.
A pre-operative review of the doctor's previous consultation by the doctor or his/her designee in which all issues related to the procedure are discussed.
A witnessed and documented discussion in which all issues discussed are initiated by the patient's questions so that the requirement to answer all of the patient's questions is clearly met.

questions.text: A patient presents to your office for extraction of a tooth. You obtain a written and oral medical history which reveals the following information: • 70-year-old male • Myocardial infarction 3 years ago • 3 stents placed at that time • Ejection fraction 50 % • Develops shortness of breath when climbing more than 1 flight of steps • Takes insulin for diabetes What ASA classification would best describe his condition?
Which of the following statements about patients with thrombocytopenia is TRUE?
options: A patient may have a platelet deficiency, but as long as their platelet count is 50,000 or more, tooth extraction can generally be performed without significant bleeding risk.

If a patient with a history of thrombocytopenia has a normal platelet count for greater than two months, it can be assumed that their platelet count will stay in the normal range and surgery can be safely performed.
If tests reveal a normal platelet count on a patient with a known platelet disorder, tooth extraction can be performed without risk of bleeding.
Liver disease is never a cause of an abnormal platelet count.
If a patient has a history of thrombocytopenia but has a normal platelet count at the time of surgery, they can be given NSAIDs or aspirin for pain control in the peri-operative period.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding management of anticoagulation with regard to the performance of oral surgery procedures is TRUE?
options: A treating dentist should always advise a patient on warfarin to not take their warfarin for three days prior to an extraction.
The decision as to whether or not to hold off on taking targeted anticoagulants prior to tooth extraction should be based on the patient's INR three days before the procedure.
The MAPPP app is extremely useful because it gives treating dentists the information they need to manage their patients' anticoagulation without ever having to consult their patients' physicians.

Decisions regarding the management of anticoagulation prior to tooth extraction should be based on the risk of bleeding with the specific procedure being performed and the risk of clotting complications if the anticoagulation therapy is interrupted. A decision to interrupt a patient's anticoagulation should be made in conjunction with the physician managing the anticoagulation.

In this day and age, it is never necessary to alter a patient's anticoagulation regimen prior to oral surgical procedures because local adjunctive procedures and materials and reversal agents can be utilized to safely control all post-operative bleeding.

questions.text: All of the following statements regarding oral surgery on patients who have conditions that may exacerbate their potential to bleed are TRUE, EXCEPT:
options: Patients with the potential to have bleeding problems should be taken care of early in the day and early in the week for elective and non-emergent situations.
If a patient with increased risk for bleeding requires multiple teeth to be extracted, it may be prudent to first perform a “test” surgery by extracting one or two teeth and seeing how they respond.
Local anesthetic that contains epinephrine should always be used on these patients as it will overcome the patient's risk for increased bleeding.
Adjunctive local measures should be utilized to reduce the risk of harmful bleeding.

When circumstances permit, oral surgical procedures should be scheduled at times when bleeding risk is less likely, such as before or after chemotherapy regimens, rather than while chemotherapy is being performed.

questions.text: Which of the following practices would NOT be useful for minimizing the risk of vaso-vagal reactions?
options: Maintaining the patient in an upright position throughout the procedure.

questions.text: Which of the following regimens is applicable for a patient with Type 1 diabetes in the peri-operative period?
options: If the patient was able to eat breakfast and their post-operative oral intake will be impaired, then the patient should take their usual dose of regular insulin and one-half of their NPH dose.
If the patient is NPO, then they should take their usual dose of regular insulin and not take their NPH dose.
If the patient was able to eat breakfast and their post-operative oral intake will be impaired, then the patient should take one half of their dose of regular insulin and their usual NPH dose.
If the patient is NPO, then they should not take their regular insulin but they should take their regular NPH dose.
Whether or not the patient is able to eat before surgery, they should follow their usual insulin regimen as prescribed by their doctor.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding oral surgery in HIV+ patients is TRUE?
options: HIV+ patients are at significantly increased risk of infection following oral surgical procedures.
Approximately 50 % of HIV+ patients have a decreased platelet count that puts them at significant risk of bleeding during and following oral surgical procedures.
Antibiotic prophylaxis is indicated for oral surgical procedures an HIV+ patient with a CD4+ count less than 200.
Antibiotic prophylaxis is indicated for oral surgical procedures for an HIV+ patient with a neutrophil count less than 4000.
HIV antiviral medications do not exhibit significant interactions with other medications that may be used by these patients.

questions.text: Which of the following statements related to osteoradionecrosis (ORN) is NOT TRUE?
options: Removal of potential sources of infection such as carious or periodontally involved teeth before the initiation of radiation treatment is helpful in the prevention of ORN.
When extractions are performed prior to irradiation, sharp areas of bone should be smoothed as bone remodeling will not occur normally in irradiated bone.
When extractions are performed prior to irradiation, primary closure of soft tissue should be achieved when possible so that radiation therapy can be initiated as soon as possible.

When extractions are performed prior to irradiation, a three-week waiting period prior to irradiation will generally be adequate. If soft tissue closure has not occurred, irradiation should be withheld until this is achieved, unless the risk of waiting longer is significant.
Endodontic treatment of non-restorable teeth in irradiated patients is not beneficial as these procedures are associated with the same risk as extractions in these patients.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding patients with adrenal suppression is TRUE?
options: Secondary adrenal suppression is caused by any disease of the adrenal cortex which results in an inability to release endogenous corticosteroids in response to stress.
Complex prolonged surgery may result in hypertension, syncope, nausea, and hypothermia.
Supplemental steroids should be given for all patients with adrenal suppression for any surgical procedure.

When supplemental steroids are necessary for a patient who is currently on steroids, the following regimen should be followed: Administer twice the patient's daily dose on pre-op, op, and post-op day 1, then resume the normal dose.

When supplemental steroids are necessary for a patient who has taken 20 mg of hydrocortisone or its equivalent for two or more weeks within the previous year, the following regimen should be followed: Administer steroids for six weeks as follows: 60 mg of hydrocortisone daily for 2 weeks before the procedure, 40 mg daily for 2 weeks following the procedure, and then 20 mg daily for the following 2 weeks.

questions.text: Several scenarios and management strategies regarding patients presenting for oral surgery are paired below. Which of the following management strategies DOES NOT MAKE SENSE for the scenario it accompanies?
options: A 22-year-old male professional bicycle racer presents with a blood pressure of 118/72 and a pulse of 48. Treatment can be provided as these vital signs do not indicate a problem for this patient. Lidocaine with epinephrine can be administered for local anesthesia.

A 16-year-old girl who weighs 101 pounds presents with a blood pressure of 97/68 and a pulse of 102. Treatment can be provided as these vital signs do not indicate a problem for this patient. Mepivaciane can be administered for local anesthesia.

A 72-year-old male with a history of hypertension presents with a blood pressure of 162/94 and a pulse of 84. Treatment can be provided as these vital signs do not indicate a problem for this patient. Either mepivacaine or up to two carpules of lidoocaine with epinephrine can be administered for local anesthesia.

A 78-year-old female with a history of hypertension presents with a blood pressure of 212/112 and a pulse of 92. She is complaining of pain in one of her maxillary molars and feels the tooth is causing her to have a headache. Treatment should not be provided at this time. The dentist should arrange for immediate evaluation and treatment of the patient's blood pressure.

An anxious 16-year-old boy presents with a blood pressure of 122/72 and a pulse of 138. Treatment can be provided as these vital signs do not indicate a problem for this patient. lidocaine with epinephrine can be administered for local anesthesia.

questions.text: A patient with a history of angina presents for extraction of a tooth. All of the following management strategies can be used by a general dentist, EXCEPT:
options: Monitor the patient's vital signs before, during, and following the procedure.
Use techniques to minimize the patient's anxiety.
Administer nitroglycerin if the patient experiences an episode of angina.
Limit or avoid epinephrine use with local anesthetics.
Refer the patient to an Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon for tooth extraction.
All of these strategies can be used.

questions.text: When treating an asthmatic patient, which of the following is NOT a helpful strategy/management technique?
options: Determine the severity and risk related to their asthma by obtaining a history including information about the frequency and severity of their episodes; whether they have presented to an Emergency Department, been hospitalized, or intubated for their asthma; what triggers their asthma; and when their most recent episode was.
If an asthma attack does occur intraoperatively, immediately administer cromolyn sodium to treat the patient.
Use a bronchodilator pre-operatively prophylactically and intra-operatively if an episode occurs.
Assess the patient for wheezing pre- and intra-operatively.
If general anesthesia is being contemplated, consult the patient's physician regarding the risks associated with the general anesthesia.
When choosing post-operative analgesics, be aware that some asthmatics have an increased risk for aspirin allergy.

questions.text: When general dentists are making decisions on the appropriate treatment for medically compromised patients that they may be taking care of, which of the following is NOT a legitimate consideration?
options: The general dentist's level of experience and expertise regarding the necessary procedure.
Relative or absolute medical contraindications to the proposed surgery or anesthesia that may necessitate a change in the planned procedures.
“Modification” of the patient's condition and/or management so that surgery may be safely performed.
Referral to an Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon may be the best option for treatment.
Consultation with the patient's physician may be necessary prior to treatment.
General dentists should never perform surgical procedures on medically compromised patients.

questions.text: Which of the following layers is NOT included in the flap when a full thickness mucoperiosteal flap (FTMPF) is elevated?
options: Mucosa, submucosa, periosteum, and bone are all included in the flap.

questions.text: When developing a full thickness mucoperiosteal flap (FTMPF) with 2 releasing incisions, the flap should be broader at the free gingival margin than at the base.
Which of the following flaps/incisions should generally NOT be used during extractions?
When making a vertical releasing incision during dentoalveolar surgery, the incision should be placed:
options: At the tip of the papilla.
At the line angle of the tooth.
Directly over the area of pathology.
Across the root just crossing the apex.
Just over or anterior to the mental foramen when extracting a mandibular bicuspid.

questions.text: It is June 2018. While extracting a tooth and doing everything the way you were taught, much to your surprise, the tooth fractures. Before calling your instructor over, you start thinking about what the best treatment would be at this time. You remember that the apical portion of a tooth can be left in place if:
options: It has a radiolucency at the apex of the root.
It is greater than 4 to 5 mm in length.
It is close to a vital structure.
The patient would have no way of ever finding out that it was there.

questions.text: Which of the following terms does NOT refer to a portion of a suture needle?
Which of the following suture materials is non-resorbable?
When penetrating a soft tissue flap with a suture needle, the angle of penetration is…
options: important and ideally it should enter the tissue perpendicular to the flap.
important and ideally it should enter the tissue at an acute angle to the flap.
important and ideally it should enter the tissue at an obtuse angle to the flap.
important, but it will vary based on the location and type of flap.
not important. It should enter the tissue at whatever angle is most comfortable for the operator.

questions.text: A flap should be designed so that all of the incisions can be closed over bone.
A surgical handpiece should be used during surgical procedures to section teeth and cut bone instead of a regular dental handpiece that is used for operative dentistry, because:
options: A surgical handpiece expels air from the rear of the handpiece to prevent air emphysema from occurring.
A surgical handpiece is longer than a regular dental handpiece, providing better access for reaching the apical portion of teeth.
A surgical handpiece expels air around the bur so that it keeps the surgical field clear, providing better visibility.
A surgical handpiece expels air around the bur so that it clears the surgical field of debris, minimizing the risk of infection.
Either a surgical handpiece or a regular dental handpiece can be used during surgical procedures.

questions.text: What happens to the alveolar bone and soft tissues after teeth are extracted?
options: The bone contour changes but the soft tissue contour does not.
The soft tissue contour changes but the bone contour does not.
Both bone and soft tissue contour changes take place.
Neither bone or soft tissue contour changes take place.
Periosteum and bone changes occur, but mucosal changes do not.

questions.text: When evaluating patients for pre-prosthetic surgery, it is always necessary to:
options: Palpate the hard and soft tissues.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding an epulis fissuratum is TRUE:
options: The etiology can be a poor fitting denture.
The etiology can be a retained root tip.
Excision of the lesion is curative.
Excision of the lesion alone is not curative - radiation is also necessary.
Excision of the lesion alone is not curative - chemotherapy is also necessary.
Excision of the lesion alone is not curative - radiation and chemotherapy are both also necessary.

questions.text: Which of the following techniques and information are routinely required by a well-trained dentist to diagnose the condition of a patient's tooth and determine what treatment options are indicated? • I. Radiographic imaging. • II. Chief complaint and related history. • III. Clinical examination. • IV. Clinical research. • V. Literature review.
Which of the following instruments are used for retracting? • I. Weider • II. Minnesota • III. Seldin • IV. 301 • V. 46R
What is a No 9 Molt periosteal elevator used for?
options: To make an incision through periosteum.
To elevate a tooth from the periodontal ligament.

questions.text: Which is the most common scalpel blade used to make an incision in oral surgery?

Your “first-day-on-the-job” dental assistant is setting up an instrument tray for you to use to extract tooth #8. He asks you in what order you like your instruments to be placed on the tray. You tell him to set them up in the order in which you will use them. Which of the following makes the most sense?
options: Scalpel, periosteal elevator, straight elevator, upper ash forceps, rongeur.
Periosteal elevator, straight elevator, rongeur, upper ash forceps.
Periosteal elevator, scalpel, straight elevator, rongeur upper ash forceps.
Scalpel, periosteal elevator, rongeur, straight elevator, upper ash forceps.
Scalpel, periosteal elevator, straight elevator, rongeur, upper ash forceps.

questions.text: It is May 2020. You are on your final TCDM Oral Surgery Rotation. Your schedule includes five patients requiring extractions as described below. Which patient/tooth scenario would you anticipate will be the MOST DIFFICULT surgical procedure that you are being asked to perform that day?
options: Extraction of endodontically treated maxillary central incisor on a 65-year-old male.
Extraction of erupted maxillary second premolar on a 12-year-old female.
Extraction of erupted maxillary third molar on a 21-year-old female.
Extraction of mandibular first molar on a 54-year-old female with MIO (maximum interincisal opening) of 10mm.
Extraction of mobile mandibular central incisor on an 85-year-old male on warfarin with an INR of 1.9.

questions.text: Which of the following is most helpful in removing and contouring bone around the socket of an extracted tooth?
A mandibular first molar with a severely carious crown is being extracted. Which of the following techniques should NOT be used in the removal of this tooth?
options: Removal of the thin lingual cortical plate of bone.
Elevation of the individual roots with east-west elevators.
Sectioning the tooth into separate mesial and distal roots.
Reflecting a modest buccal flap and removing the most minimal amount of buccal bone necessary to accomplish the extraction.

questions.text: Which of the following teeth must be luxated buccal-lingually to minimize the risk of fracture of the roots during extraction?

A mandibular molar is fractured during extraction. The entire mesial root and the superior portion of the distal root are removed with the crown. The remaining one third of the distal root is visualized in its original position. What is the best instrument for removal of this fragment?
options: Either a North or South elevator, depending if the tooth is on the left or right side of the mandible.

questions.text: Which of the following teeth are most susceptible to root fracture during extraction?
Dental elevators are single blade instruments that are:
options: Used to reflect gingiva prior to the application of the dental forceps.
Designed to engage the tooth apical to the cemento-enamel junction.
Designed to engage the tooth coronal to the cemento-enamel junction.
Used to reflect a full thickness mucoperiosteal flap prior to application of the dental forceps.
Designed to mobilize the tooth by using an adjacent tooth as a fulcrum.

questions.text: The beaks of a needle holder are ______________ than the beaks of a hemostat.
Which of the following instruments is the best choice for grasping soft tissue during various oral surgical procedures such as suturing?
Consider the following radiograph: What is the indication for removal of tooth #31shown in this radiograph?
options: Bone loss in furcation due to probable fracture or perforation and/or periodontal issue.
Extraction is not indicated as there does not appear to be any pathology associated with this tooth.

questions.text: (Bonus Question) You are on your Oral Surgery Rotation at Touro Dental Health. An emergency patient presents complaining of several days of pain of increasing severity from a carious non-restorable tooth. You review the patient's medical history, obtain informed consent, and administer mepivacaine so that you may perform an extraction. As you are about to begin the extraction, the patient's wife comes in and asks the patient if he remembered to tell you that he started warfarin several weeks ago for atrial fibrillation. You want to help the patient out so you:
options: Extract the tooth, supplementing the mepivacaine with lidocaine with epinephrine to minimize bleeding, tell the patient not to take his warfarin for three days, and give him detailed post-operative instructions regarding bleeding control. Advise the patient to take acetaminophen for his post-operative pain.
Tell the patient to take ibuprofen for his pain and not take his warfarin for three days and re-schedule the extraction in three days.
Tell the patient to take acetaminophen for his pain and not take his warfarin for three days and re-schedule the extraction in three days.

Call the patient's physician to see if he knows the patient's platelet count. Based on this information decide with the physician how to manage the patient's warfarin and when to perform the extraction. Advise the patient to take acetaminophen for his pain.

Check the patient's INR and find out that it is 2.0. Tell the patient it is his lucky day. Proceed with the extraction and take local measures to maximize hemostasis. Advise the patient to take acetaminophen for his post-operative pain.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an essential element of the informed consent process?
options: Likelihood of success of the planned procedure.
Assurances that the procedure will go well.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT TRUE when obtaining a patient's medical history?
options: Using a written health history can be an effective method for obtaining a patient's medical history.
Using an oral history can be an effective method for obtaining a patient's medical history.
When evaluating the information that a patient provides, it is important to consider how accurate an historian he/she is.
When evaluating the information that a patient provides, it is important to consider whether they realize any secondary gain by providing incomplete or inaccurate information.
Redundant questioning will not yield any additional information.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about ASA classifications is CORRECT?
options: This classification system was put forth by the American Society of Anesthesiologists and should only be applied to patients who will be receiving anesthesia.
Patients who are classified as ASA V and ASA VI are routinely treated in the dental setting.
Patients who are classified as ASA IV have mild systemic disease or a significant health risk factor.
Patients who are classified as ASA II have severe systemic life-threatening disease.
Patients who are classified as ASA III have severe systemic disease that is incapacitating.

questions.text: Questioning a patient about which of the following areas may be helpful in assessing a patient's risk for bleeding?
Which of the following statements regarding patients with various conditions that put them at risk for bleeding is NOT TRUE?
options: DDAVP (desmopressin) nasal administration can be effective in increasing a patient's levels of VWF and Factor VIII.
Use of aminocaproic acid may help prevent clot breakdown in at-risk patients.
Once a patient's platelet count is 100,000 or less, they are at significant risk of bleeding with any surgical procedure and require platelet supplementation.
DDAVP (desmopressin) and corticosteroids can be effective in increasing a patient's levels of platelets.
Strict adherence to post-operative instructions will lessen the chance of significant bleeding occurring.

questions.text: Which of the following conditions should NOT make a dentist suspicious that the patient may be on anticoagulation therapy?
options: Patients with need for extracorporeal blood flow - dialysis.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is NOT TRUE regarding target specific anticoagulants?
options: They generally should be discontinued prior to oral surgery, even for procedures with low bleeding risk.
Their pharmacokinetics are more predictable than warfarin.
Their half-lives are shorter than the half-life of warfarin.
Their use requires little to no routine monitoring
They exhibit fewer drug or food interactions than are seen with warfarin.

questions.text: Which of the following studies are NOT useful in assessing a patient's potential for hemostasis?

Which of the following plans makes sense to implement prior to performing oral surgery on an anticoagulated patient? (Assume that the anticoagulants stated in the answer are the only anticoagulants that the patient is on and that all of the plans are developed in consultation with patient's physician.)
options: Discontinue aspirin and Plavix one day prior to the surgery.
If the patient's INR is 2.0 or less, discontinue the warfarin for three days prior to the surgery.
If the patient's INR is 5.3 and emergency surgery is necessary, consider using protamine sulfate to reverse the effects of the warfarin.

A patient on warfarin with a high risk of developing clots is undergoing a procedure with a high risk of bleeding. Check the INR and discontinue the warfarin three days before the procedure. Administer enoxaparin (Lovenox) (low molecular weight heparin) to maintain anticoagulation and discontinue the enoxaprin pre-operatively. Resume the enoxaprin and warfarin following the surgery. Discontinue the enoxaprin when the INR has returned to its therapeutic level.
If the patient is on a target specific anticoagulant, check the INR daily beginning one week before the oral surgery to determine when the medication should be stopped.

questions.text: Which of the following techniques should NOT be utilized for the management of “potential bleeders”?
options: They should be treated early in the day and early in the week.
If possible, oral surgery procedures should be performed prior to initiation of any therapies that would cause a higher potential for bleeding.

Consider doing a “test surgery” - extracting a single tooth rather that several teeth at once to see how the patient responds. Additionally, if a bleeding problem does occur, it would be less critical as it is from a single, smaller area and easier to manage.
Use adjunctive local measures to minimize the potential to bleed.
Patients undergoing dialysis should be treated on the day of their dialysis.

questions.text: All of the following may be useful in minimizing the chances of a patient having a vaso-vagal reaction, EXCEPT:
options: Being aware of a patient's previous history of having vaso-vagal reactions and being extra diligent with all possible preventative measures.
Treating the patient in an upright position.

questions.text: Which of the following conditions is/are accompanied by an increased risk of infection?
options: Immunologic diseases that are congenital or acquired.
All of the answer choices in this question are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE when comparing diabetic patients to patients without diabetes?
options: Well-controlled diabetics do not have an increased risk of infection, but if they develop an infection, it is more difficult to control.
Poorly controlled diabetics do not have an increased risk of infection, but if they develop an infection, it is more difficult to control.
Well-controlled diabetics have an increased risk of infection and if they develop an infection it is more difficult to control.
Patients with diabetes do not show any difference in the risk of developing an infection or controlling an infection when compared to patients without diabetes.
Prophylactic antibiotics should be given to all diabetic patients undergoing oral surgery no matter what level of control they maintain.

questions.text: Which of the following management strategies is NOT a useful strategy for managing diabetic patients?
options: Consult the patient's physician as necessary.
During the immediate perioperative period, mild-moderate hyperglycemia is preferred over hypoglycemia.
The decision to administer antibiotics is based on specific systemic and local factors related to the patient's condition and the surgery being performed.
If possible, surgical treatment should be delayed until a diabetic patient's condition is optimized.
A patient's normal regimen of hypoglycemic medications should be always be strictly adhered to during the pre- and post- operative periods in order to maintain optimal glucose control.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a sign or symptom of hypoglycemia?
Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding HIV+ patients?
options: Approximately 1/5 of HIV+ patients exhibit a clinically significant decrease in platelets which will result in bleeding problems during oral surgery procedures.
All patients with a CD4+ T cell count above 100 do not require prophylactic antibiotics for oral surgery.
All patients with a neutrophil count less than 1000 require prophylactic antibiotics for oral surgery.
Studies show that all HIV+ patients are at increased risk of infection when undergoing oral surgery procedures.
Acetaminophen may have an unfavorable interaction with the HIV drug zidovudine (Retrovir) which can intensify granulocytopenia and anemia in these patients.

questions.text: All of the following statements regarding the use of antibiotic prophylaxis are TRUE, EXCEPT:
options: All patients who have had joint replacements require antibiotic prophylaxis when undergoing oral surgery procedures.
All patients with cardiac valve replacements require antibiotic prophylaxis when undergoing oral surgery procedures.

If a patient who requires antibiotic prophylaxis for an oral surgery procedure is already on an antibiotic, an antibiotic from another class should be administered for the prophylaxis to reduce the risk from resistant organisms.
Certain cardiac valve conditions may require antibiotic prophylaxis for oral surgery procedures.
Prescribing prophylactic antibiotics when they are not indicated can result in health risks for the patient and development of resistant bacteria.

questions.text: Which of the following statements related to ORN (osteoradionecrosis) is NOT TRUE?
options: Removal of teeth which have a poor prognosis should be accomplished prior to starting radiation treatment.
ORN risk is higher in the denser mandible when compared to the maxilla due to increased bone devitalization in the at-risk mandible.

A total radiation treatment dose below 5000 rad (50 Gy) has decreased ORN risk when compared to higher doses. This is significant because 90% of oral malignancies are squamous cell carcinomas which require radiation doses exceeding 6000 rad (60 Gy).
Pre-irradiation extractions should be done in as simple a fashion as possible with minimal bone removal to allow bone remodeling to occur in a natural manner.

HBO (hyperbaric oxygen) may be a useful adjunctive therapy when it is necessary to perform oral surgery in patients who are at risk for ORN (osteoradionecrosis) due to radiation to the head and neck region.

questions.text: In an adrenally suppressed patient, complex prolonged surgery may cause adrenal crisis. Which of the following is NOT a potential sign, symptom or result of adrenal crisis?
Which of the following statements regarding the management of adrenally suppressed patients is NOT TRUE?
options: Use measures to minimize their anxiety in the peri-operative period.
Monitor HR/BP intra- and post-op &other signs/symptoms of adrenal crisis
Administer supplemental steroids for all dental procedures.
For a patient currently on steroids, supplemental steroids should be administered as follows: Give 2X daily dose on pre-op, op, &post-op day 1, then resume daily dose.

For a patient who has had 20 mg hydrocortisone for >or = 2 weeks within past year: Use a “steroid taper” as follows: Give 60 mg hydrocortisone on pre-op and op days Give 40 mg hydrocortisone on post-op days 1 &2 Give 20 mg hydrocortisone on post-op days 3,4, &5.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding patients with hypertension is NOT TRUE?
options: Avoid rapid positional changes in hypertensive patients on vasodilators.
Blood pressure measurements with systolic pressure above 140 but below 200 and diastolic pressure above 90 but below 140 are considered to be in the mild/moderate hypertension range.
Every attempt should be made to achieve a “normal textbook” blood pressure, approximately 120/80, in all patients on whom oral surgery is being performed.

Patients with severe hypertension should not be provided with dental treatment when they present to a dental office. Instead, they should immediately be referred to their primary care physician or an Emergency Department for evaluation and treatment..
Patients with severe hypertension are at risk for CVA (cerebrovascular accident, a.k.a. stroke).

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding a patient's heart rate is TRUE?
options: Normal heart rate is considered anywhere between 50 and 110.

If a patient's heart rate is lower than what is considered within the normal range, the patient clearly has a medical problem and should receive appropriate treatment before dental treatment is performed.
Increased heart rate can occur due to a substance that has been ingested, a heart rhythm abnormality, or a patient being a “trained athlete”.
Epinephrine may cause an increase in a patient's heart rate.
Decreased heart rate can occur due to a heart rhythm abnormality, pain, or anxiety.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding patients with cardiac issues is NOT TRUE?
options: If a patient tells you that they have had a coronary artery stent placed, you can conclude that they have had a myocardial infarction.
If circumstances allow, it may be prudent to delay dental treatment during the period following a myocardial infarction.
In a patient with angina pectoris, nitroglycerin can be used prior to dental treatment to reduce the chances of an episode occurring.
Generally, patients with congestive heart failure should not be placed in the supine position during dental treatment.
Anxiety reduction, supplemental O2, and limiting the amount of epinephrine administered with local anesthesia may all be useful techniques when treating patients with cardiac issues.

questions.text: Radiographs of 5 teeth are shown below. Which of these teeth do you anticipate would be the ”EASIEST” one to extract?
Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: A full thickness mucoperiosteal flap involves the elevation of periosteum, submucosa, and mucosa.
A full thickness mucoperiosteal flap involves the elevation of submucosa and mucosa.
A full thickness mucoperiosteal flap involves the elevation of periosteum and submucosa.
A partial thickness mucoperiosteal flap involves the elevation of periosteum and mucosa.
A partial thickness mucoperiosteal flap involves the elevation of periosteum, submucosa, and mucosa.

questions.text: There are several principles that should be adhered to when planning and developing a flap. Which of the following concepts regarding flap design is FALSE?
options: The free margin of the flap should be broader than the base.
The flap should be of proper size to allow for adequate visualization.
Releasing incisions should be used only when necessary.
Injury to vital structures in the area should be avoided.
Flaps should be closed over sound bone.

questions.text: Several flap designs are displayed in the picture below. Which line shows a flap with two vertical releases that has been properly designed to respect all principles of flap design?
Which of the following statements is TRUE concerning envelope, 3 corner, and 4 corner flaps?
options: The 3 corner flap is developed using 2 vertical releasing incisions.
The 4 corner flap is developed using 2 vertical releasing incisions.
The envelope flap is developed using 1 vertical releasing incision.
The 3 corner flap is developed using 3 vertical releasing incisions.
The 4 corner flap is developed using 4 vertical releasing incisions.

questions.text: Which of the following should be considered when making a decision as to whether or not a root fragment can be left in?
options: The proximity of the root to the maxillary sinus.
The proximity of the root to the inferior alveolar nerve canal.
The presence or absence of periapical radiolucency at the root apex.
The anticipated prosthetic treatment plan including possible implant placement.

questions.text: Bone and soft tissue changes which occur after tooth extraction are affected by all of the following systemic and local factors, EXCEPT:
options: Flap design and elevation techniques utilized at the time of the extractions.
Alveoplasty techniques utilized at the time of the extractions.
Distribution of occlusal forces on the denture the patient is wearing.
All of the choices in this answer are factors that affect bone and soft tissue changes.

questions.text: A determination as to whether or not preprosthetic surgery is necessary is based on the evaluation of the patient's oral hard and soft tissues. The following factors are all important to assess during the soft tissue evaluation, EXCEPT:
options: Ulcerations from existing ill-fitting dentures or overlying boney protuberances.
Pneumatization of posterior maxilla by maxillary sinus.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements regarding alveoplasty procedures is FALSE?
options: Bone can be removed/recontoured with a handpiece/bur.
One goal of an alveoplasty is to eliminate bony interferences with denture insertion.
One goal of an alveoplasty is to eliminate bony protuberances which may cause discomfort under a removable prosthesis.
Bone can be removed/recontoured with a rongeur and/or a bone file.

When doing an alveoplasty, the operator should palpate for any remaining sharp boney areas which may irritate the patient by moving his/her finger directly over the surface of the bone underneath the flap.

questions.text: Excessive size of the maxillary tuberosity might interfere with removable prosthesis fabrication and use. Tuberosity reduction may be performed to eliminate this problem. Which of the following statements regarding tuberosity reduction is FALSE?
options: Under some circumstances, tuberosity reduction may be successfully accomplished by bone removal only.
Under some circumstances, tuberosity reduction may be successfully accomplished by soft tissue removal only.
Under some circumstances, tuberosity reduction may be successfully accomplished by a combination of both soft tissue and bone removal.
The informed consent discussion prior to tuberosity reduction procedures should include the potential post-procedure risk of an oro-antral communication.
The informed consent discussion prior to tuberosity reduction procedures should include the potential post-procedure risk of a neurosensory disturbance of upper lip.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding torus reduction/removal is TRUE?
options: If a patient has pain or ulceration overlying a torus following insertion of a removable prosthesis, accommodation will occur and the torus will not need to be removed.
Either a “y” or „double Y” incision can be utilized when reducing/removing a mandibular torus.
When performing the reduction/removal of a mandibular torus, excessive bleeding or swelling which may ultimately cause airway compromise is a potential complication.
Since reduction/removal of mandibular tori is a procedure that has very little risk, these tori should always be removed when a removable prosthesis is being fabricated.
A horizontal incision across a maxillary torus should be utilized when reducing/removing the torus.

questions.text: The steps below are all involved in a combination labial vestibuloplasty, floor-of-mouth lowering procedure and skin grafting (i.e. Obwegeser technique), but are NOT necessarily listed in the correct order. (1) Place skin graft over the supraperiosteal dissection. (2) Tether the labial and lingual flaps near the inferior border of the mandible by passing sutures under the inferior border of the mandible. (3) Make a crestal incision. The labiovestibular mucosa is sutured to the periosteum of the remaining maxilla.
Adequate mucosal length must be available in this area to provide adequate vestibular depth without producing an abnormal appearance of the upper lip.
To determine whether adequate labiovestibular mucosa is present a dental mouth mirror is used under the upper lip to elevate the superior aspect of the vestibule to the desired postoperative depth.
All of the answers listed here are true.

Premolars are always extracted to create space in a crowded arch.
All impacted third molars should be extracted to prevent pathology.

Which of the following statements regarding alveoplasty procedures is FALSE?
options: Simple alveoplasty utilizes a buccal flap to adequately expose the buccal bone.
Intraseptal alveoplasty does not utilize a buccal flap to expose the buccal bone.
A disadvantage of an intraseptal alveoplasty is that the ridge width is lessened.
A simple alveoplasty works well to contour irregularities of the buccal bone.
Alveoplasty procedures must be utilized to eliminate all bony undercuts.

questions.text: Whenever a tuberosity reduction is performed, bone and soft tissue must both be removed.
Which of the following statements regarding the removal of inflamed fibrous hyperplastic soft tissue such as an epulis is FALSE?
options: When a small, well-localized area of fibrous hyperplasia is excised, simple closure of the mucosal wound margins should be performed.
When a large area of inflammatory fibrous hyperplasia is excised, primary closure of mucosal tissues would result in reduction or elimination of the labial vestibule.

When a large area of inflammatory fibrous hyperplasia is excised, supraperiosteal removal followed by suturing of the mucosal edge to the periosteum at the depth of the vestibule should be performed to preserve the labial vestibule.
The amount of tissue excised determines the depth of the labial vestibule.  Suture technique does not have any effect on this depth.

questions.text: Which of the following statements (A, B, C, D) about frenectomy procedures is FALSE?
options: This procedure may be done with a laser.
Suture techniques can influence the final result.
The Z-plasty technique involves additional incisions after the frenum is excised with the intent of decreasing loss of vestibular depth.
Frenectomy may be useful in reducing denture displacement.
None of the statements (A, B, C, D) are FALSE. All of the statements (A, B, C, D) are TRUE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the Transpositional Flap Vestibuloplasty, also known as the Lip Switch Procedure, is NOT TRUE?
options: Bone height of at least 5 mm is required for this procedure to be useful.
If adequate lingual vestibular depth is not present, this procedure will not be useful.
This procedure involves a supra-periosteal dissection along the anterior aspect of the mandible.
The exposed labial tissue heals by secondary intention.
Disadvantages of the procedure include possible relapse and vestibular scarring.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding Immediate Denture techniques for a full upper denture is FALSE?
options: Posterior teeth should be extracted initially with adequate time allowed for healing prior to denture fabrication.
Immediate Dentures allow patients to maintain their anterior teeth for esthetic and psychological benefits until their dentures are inserted.
Final ridge form is simulated by removing the teeth to be extracted on the final models prior to denture fabrication.
This technique can utilize either digital or conventional analog impressions.
Dentures should be inserted and adjusted when the anterior teeth are removed and then left out for at least one week to allow for healing.

questions.text: Which of the conclusions to the following sentence are FALSE: The purpose of this course is to teach dental students about Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery so that as general practitioners, you can:
options: understand what oral surgical treatments are available for your patients.
understand the risks and benefits of oral surgical procedures that your patients may undergo.
understand the post-operative course for your patients following various oral surgical procedures.
perform any oral surgical procedure that your patients may need.
talk to your patients about oral surgical procedures.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about obtaining a medical history is FALSE?
options: Asking questions that seem redundant may yield different information.
Medical history should be updated for all patients once a year.
Asking age-appropriate questions to children and adolescents when they are separated from their parent/guardian may yield important information that was not obtained from the parent/guardian.
Patients’ health literacy must be considered when interpreting answers.
Patients may realize secondary gain by misinforming the history taker.

questions.text: It’s 3 months from now and (hopefully) you are seeing your first TDH clinic patient.  They get impatient waiting for the elevator so they take the stairs.  They climb one flight, stopping along the way.  They continue to clinic on the elevator. You question them and learn that they have coronary artery disease with stents placed 3 months prior.  They also have poorly controlled diabetes. Which ASA classification describes this patient:
Which of the following does NOT have an effect on a patient’s hemostasis status?
options: Use of NSAIDs such as ibuprofen.

questions.text: Which of the following statements (A, B, C, D) is TRUE?
options: Target specific oral anticoagulants should always be discontinued prior to performing dental extractions.
Patients on antiplatelet therapy such as baby aspirin (81 mg) and/or clopidogrel should always stop these medications prior to undergoing dental extractions.
Warfarin should always be discontinued 3 days prior to dental extractions.
Patients on heparin for dialysis should always have their INR checked prior to undergoing extractions.
None of the statements (A, B, C, D) are TRUE. All of the statements (A, B, C, D) are FALSE.

questions.text: Which of these statements regarding platelets is FALSE?
options: Patients may have bleeding issues after extractions due to quantitative problems with their platelets.
Patients may have bleeding issues after extractions due to qualitative problems with their platelets.

Normal platelet count ranges from 150,000 to 450,000 platelets per microliter of blood. If a patient has fewer than 100,000 platelets per microliter, platelet transfusions should be given before extractions or abnormal bleeding will occur.
Timing of surgical procedures for patients with a history of qualitative platelet issues may be critical as this condition is often episodic.
Administration of DDAVP and/or corticosteroids may increase platelet levels.

questions.text: The following management techniques are all recommended when treating diabetics, EXCEPT:
options: Administration of prophylactic antibiotics before all surgical procedures.
Preference for patients to have mild to moderate hyperglycemia rather than hypoglycemia during surgical procedures.
Delay elective surgical procedures until poorly controlled diabetic patients are better controlled.
Patients’ insulin doses should be adjusted based on pre-op intake and anticipated post-op intake.
Patients should be observed for signs of hypoglycemia during procedures.  These signs may include hypotension, hunger, drowsiness, nausea, diaphoresis, tachycardia, and mood change.

questions.text: Which of the following statements pertaining to HIV+ patients is TRUE?
options: About 1/5 of HIV+ patients have a decreased platelet count which puts them at significant risk of bleeding during and/or after oral surgical procedures.
Prophylactic antibiotics should be administered to all HIV+ patients prior to oral surgical procedures because they have an increased risk of developing post-operative infections.
Prophylactic antibiotics should be administered to HIV+ patients with a CD4+ T cell count <700 prior to oral surgical procedures.
Prophylactic antibiotics should be administered to HIV+ patients with a neutrophil count <500 prior to oral surgical procedures.

A decision to administer prophylactic antibiotics to HIV+ patients prior to oral surgical procedures should be based solely on their HIV status and should not take into account any other conditions that they may have.

questions.text: All of the following are potential risks or problems with unnecessary prescribing of antibiotics, EXCEPT:
options: All of these are potential risks or problems.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the management of patients who are having or have had chemotherapy or radiation therapy is TRUE?
options: Patients who are having or have had chemotherapy or radiation therapy all have the same risk for developing infections following oral surgical procedures.
Patients who have had radiation treatment are more prone to infections including ORN (osteoradionecrosis) following oral surgical procedures in the maxilla than the mandible.

Patients with a history of chemotherapy will generally exhibit a reduction or elimination of their risk for infection following oral surgical procedures after the chemotherapy is stopped and their hematopoietic system has been allowed to recover.
The risk of infection following oral surgical procedures in patients who have had radiation therapy is not related to the dose or field of the radiation.
In patients undergoing pre-irradiation extractions, the teeth should be removed as simply as possible without reduction of sharp areas and without achieving primary soft tissue closure.

questions.text: Which of the following statements made by an asthmatic patient may make you think that they are at increased risk of having an “asthma attack” during treatment?
options: “The frequency of my asthma attacks has decreased since I was a child.”
“I have never needed to go to the Emergency Room for my asthma.”
“My asthma attacks only occur when I exercise.”
“I have only been intubated for my asthma twice in the past year.”
None of these statements would make you think that your patient is at increased risk of having an “asthma attack”.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: It may be problematic if a patient’s blood pressure and/or heart rate is significantly higher or lower than their baseline values.
Patients with congestive heart failure should not be placed in the supine position.
Epinephrine may increase a patient’s heart rate and/or blood pressure.
If a patient tells you that they had cardiac stents placed, you know that they had a myocardial infarction.
Patients with atrial fibrillation are often anticoagulated.

questions.text: What is the most important piece of information to gather during your patient assessment directly from your patient?

options: Tooth 9 which is class I mobile due to traumatic occlusion.

Tooth 6 with class III+ mobility and chronic severe localized periodontal disease.
Tooth 32 with associated operculum and pericoronitis.

questions.text: In which of the following patient scenarios would an extraction be possibly contraindicated?
options: 72-year-old male with a recent history of stage IV oropharyngeal cancer who had head and neck radiation therapy in the area of the maxilla and mandible 10 months ago.
28-year-old female with pericoronitis of tooth 17 who is 8 weeks pregnant (i.e. in her first trimester).
56-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease and now controlled hypertension on enalapril and aspirin.

questions.text: Please assess this scenario and determine whether this would be a complicated or uncomplicated tooth extraction: 33-year-old female, otherwise healthy, presents with a partial bony impacted tooth 16. There is a distal operculum with some localized irritation and one of the mesial cusps is visible.

Semi-supine or supine with elbows at 90 degrees to enable maximum mobility.
Trendelenberg to enable full direct visualization of the surgical site.

questions.text: You extracted tooth 4 on a 55-year-old with no significant medical history. He has had multiple extractions in the past without any complication. You call him that evening to check and see how he’s doing. He reports that he’s still bleeding from the surgical site, but it’s not profuse and asks you what he should do. options: Tell him to go to the nearest hospital Emergency Department immediately.
Tell him to go see his physician to get a coagulation panel to find out whether he has any underlying blood dyscrasias.
Find out whether he is using his gauze packs properly and instruct him to place gauze with firm pressure at the site for 45-60 minutes.
Assume that he has been following all post-operative instructions properly and instruct him to immediately place a black tea bag at the site for 1.5 hours to help with hemostasis.
Tell him to begin rinsing with 100% hydrogen peroxide mouth rinse to constrict the vasculature at the extraction site to aid in hemostasis.

questions.text: You have a 36-year-old female in your chair and have attempted to extract tooth 14. Unfortunately, the crown fractured off and you must convert to a surgical extraction with a flap for access. Which of the following is true?
options: You should create a split thickness mucoperiosteal flap that can be sulcular or have one or two releasing incisions if necessary.

You should create a full thickness mucoperiosteal flap that includes reflection of periosteum which when sutured back will aid in bony healing.
You should create a split thickness mucoperiosteal flap that includes reflection of periosteum which when sutured back will aid in bony healing.
You should create a 6-cornered flap to optimize visibility and access to the surgical site.

questions.text: Which of the following flaps is the most appropriate flap to make given the clinical scenario?
options: You are extracting tooth 32. You create a flap with a lingual releasing incision.

questions.text: Which of the following flaps is the most appropriate flap to make given the clinical scenario?
options: You are extracting tooth 9. You create a three-cornered flap with your vertical release beginning directly on the facial aspect of tooth 9.
You are extracting tooth 5. You create a three-cornered flap with your vertical releasing incision directly on the papilla between teeth 5, 6.

You are extracting tooth 3. You create a four-cornered flap with one vertical release crossing the free gingival margin at the line angle of tooth 2 and one vertical release directly across the papilla of tooth 4.
You are extracting tooth 27. You create a three-cornered flap with your vertical release crossing the free gingival margin at the line angle of tooth 26.
You are extracting tooth 23. You create a four-cornered flap with the free margin broader than the base.

Buccal-lingually, going all the way through the tooth to the lingual cortex.
