questions.text: Which of the following teeth extractions will likely require surgical sectioning during your procedure?
options: Tooth 19 with significant bone loss and class II mobility.
Tooth 9 with some carious decay, but crown is mostly intact. There is no periodontal bone loss.
Tooth 18 with bulbous widely separated roots and minimal crown structure left.
Tooth 16 fully erupted with small conical roots and buccally malpositioned.
Tooth 24 fully erupted with pulpal necrosis.

questions.text: Which of the following statements related to ASA Classification is FALSE?
options: Anxiety can move a patient who would otherwise be ASA I to ASA II.
Smoking can move a patient who would otherwise be ASA I to ASA III.
Modifiers E and P following the ASA number indicate that the patient is undergoing an emergency procedure or is pregnant, respectively.
A patient who can climb one flight of stairs or walk two level city blocks but will need to stop enroute because of distress will generally be considered ASA III.
A patient with more than three months of angina pectoris has an ASA classification indicating that they are healthier than a patient with less than three months of unstable angina pectoris.

questions.text: Consider the following statements: I.    DDAVP (desmopressin) can be administered intranasally. II.   DDAVP administration can increase circulating levels of von Willebrand factor and Factor VIII. III.  Corticosteroid administration can increase circulating levels of clotting factors. IV.  DDAVP and corticosteroid administration can increase circulating levels of platelets.
options: I, II, III, and IV are TRUE.
II, III, and IV are TRUE.

questions.text: Patients may be anticoagulated for all of the following conditions, EXCEPT:
Which of the following statements are TRUE?
options: The effects of target specific oral anticoagulants are often altered due to food and drug interactions.
INR monitoring is used to determine dosing of target specific oral anticoagulants.
The effects of target specific oral anticoagulants can be reversed prior to oral surgery procedures with Vitamin K administration.
The effects of target specific oral anticoagulants can be reversed prior to oral surgery procedures with protamine sulfate administration.

It is generally not necessary to interrupt therapy with target specific oral anticoagulants for low bleeding risk oral surgery procedures such as extraction of fewer than three contiguous teeth, implant placement, and periodontal surgery.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are TRUE?
options: Dentists should adjust their patients’ anticoagulant medications on their own prior to minor oral surgery procedures.
Dentists should adjust their patients’ anticoagulant medications on their own prior to all oral surgery procedures.

Dentists should not adjust their patients’ anticoagulant medications on their own. Any decisions to adjust a patient’s medications should be made in conjunction with the physician who prescribed the medication.
If an anticoagulated patient has had bleeding problems after any previous oral surgery procedure, their dentist should make sure that they stop the anticoagulant prior to any subsequent oral surgery.
The decision as to whether or not to adjust a patient’s anticoagulation prior to oral surgery should be made by the patient depending on their willingness to tolerate prolonged bleeding.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are FALSE?
options: The oral surgical treatment plan for any patient is solely based on the intraoral and extraoral physical examinations and radiographic examinations, as well as the patient’s desired results.
When determining what treatment a patient needs, the surgeon needs to consider the diagnosis, differential diagnosis, or a “rule-out”.
Surgeons must use their judgement to determine when to treat and when not to treat a given patient.

All dentists should have an understanding of what oral surgical treatments are available for their patients, as well as what is involved in those treatments and the risks and benefits of those treatments.
When obtaining a medical history from a patient, it is beneficial to use questions that may seem redundant.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about updating a medical history are FALSE?
options: A patient’s medical history should be updated regularly every six months.
When updating a patient’s medical history, the depth of the discussion may vary depending on when the patient was last seen.
When updating a patient’s medical history, the depth of the discussion may vary depending on the nature of the appointment.
When updating a patient’s medical history, the depth of the discussion may vary depending on the patient’s previous medical conditions and history.
A parent may not necessarily provide an accurate medical history regarding their child.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about diabetic patients is TRUE?
options: Compared to patients without diabetes, poorly controlled diabetics do not have an increased risk of developing an infection, but if they do develop an infection, it is more difficult to control.
If a diabetic patient cannot eat before surgery but can eat normally after surgery, their insulin doses do not require any adjustments.
Signs of hypoglycemia in a diabetic patient include a decrease in pulse rate and an increase in blood pressure.
In patients with elevated HbA1c values, infection risk increases with higher values.
HbA1c values reflect glycemic control over the previous 6 months.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about HIV+ patients is TRUE?
options: About 20 % of HIV+ patients have a clinically significant decrease in platelets.
All HIV+ patients have an increased risk of infection following oral surgical procedures.
Antibiotic prophylaxis is necessary for oral surgical procedures in HIV+ patients who have CD4+ Tcell counts less than 200.
Antibiotic prophylaxis is necessary for oral surgical procedures in HIV+ patients who have neutrophil counts less than 1000.
All HIV+ patients require antibiotic prophylaxis for oral surgery procedures.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding radiation therapy in patients is FALSE?
options: Osteoradionecrosis risk is greater in the maxilla than the mandible.
Differences in osteoradionecrosis risk between the maxilla and mandible are attributed to differences in vascularity between the two jaws.
Oral squamous cell carcinoma generally requires radiation > 6000 rad (60 Gy) for treatment.
Prior to radiation therapy, extractions are often performed with increased bone removal and smoothing to allow primary soft tissue closure.
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be useful when extractions must be performed in irradiated jaws.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: When treating a patient, dentists should be more concerned with the patient’s blood pressure than with their heart rate.
When treating a patient, dentists should be more concerned with the patient’s heart rate than with their blood pressure.
If a patient’s heart rate is greater than 100, this could be because they are a “trained athlete.”
If a patient is on a medication that slows their heart rate to a value below normal, the medication should be stopped prior to oral surgery procedures.
None of these statements are TRUE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements related to blood pressure is TRUE?
options: Blood pressure values that are in the “normotensive” range (around 120/80) should be achieved in all patients prior to any oral surgery procedures are performed.

If a patient presents with blood pressure of 200/110 but reports that they do not have high blood pressure but that their pressure is elevated because they are very anxious about their anticipated procedure, it is safe to proceed with oral surgery.
Rapid positional changes should be avoided in patients on certain anti-hypertensive medications since orthostatic hypotension may occur.
Medications which reduce a patient’s anxiety do not have any effect on an anxious patient’s blood pressure at dental appointments.
One of the causes of loss of consciousness during a vaso-vagal episode is a sudden extreme increase in blood pressure.

questions.text: Consider the following radiograph: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: It is an acceptable radiograph to use prior to extracting the tooth with the “X” on it.
It is NOT an acceptable radiograph to use prior to extracting the tooth with the “X” on it.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: If a patient is going to undergo radiation therapy with exposure of the jaws and oral cavity, extraction of teeth that would otherwise be amenable to restorative and periodontal treatment may be indicated before the radiation is done.
All impacted teeth do not need to be extracted.
Trismus due to a dentoalveolar infection may make it necessary to achieve resolution of an acute infection with antibiotic therapy prior to extracting the offending tooth.
Extraction of third molars with severe active pericoronitis is associated with an increased incidence of post-operative complications.
All of these statements are TRUE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: It is not important to know the restorative treatment plan when extracting a tooth.
Extensive bone pathology distant to a tooth being extracted does not complicate the extraction.
The condition of a tooth adjacent to a tooth to be extracted does not influence whether or not an extraction is complicated.
A patient’s medical status does not influence whether or not an extraction is complicated.
All of these statements are FALSE.

questions.text: Assume that the maxillary first molar indicated with the “X” that is shown in this radiograph requires extraction. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: It is likely that this tooth can be removed with a closed extraction technique.
The restoration in the adjacent premolar should be removed prior to the first molar extraction to prevent fracture of the premolar.
Although it is unlikely that this tooth can be removed with a closed extraction technique, the closed technique should be used in case the surgeon gets lucky.
The closed extraction technique should be used until the tooth fractures and then an open technique should be used to remove whatever portion of the tooth remains.
An open extraction technique should be used from the start.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about forceps is TRUE?
options: It is important to use the correct forceps when extracting a tooth since the beaks of the forceps were designed to adapt to the crown of the tooth.
The beaks of the forceps should be seated as apically as possible on the tooth being extracted.
When extracting a tooth, the beaks of the forceps should be parallel to the tooth in the buccal-lingual plane but this is not necessary in the mesial-distal plane.
The position and angulation of the beaks of the forceps is not important when extracting a tooth.
The maxillary universal forceps is also called a 151 forceps.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about different forces and pressures that are applied during tooth extraction is FALSE?
options: When extracting a tooth, pressure is directed in the apical direction, even though the ultimate goal is to move the tooth in the opposite direction.
Rotational forces are most effective when applied to teeth that have single conical roots.
The use of excessive force when applying buccal pressure can result in fracture of the buccal plate of bone or the tooth.
Tractional force should be a strong force as it is the final and ultimate force that removes the tooth.
All of these statements are TRUE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about luxation is FALSE?
options: During extractions, teeth are luxated with both elevators and forceps.
When luxating a tooth with forceps, the tooth should be held for a few seconds at maximum luxation position.
Most teeth are delivered with a final luxation movement towards the lingual/palatal direction.
Luxation movements may be increased in magnitude as increased mobility is achieved.
Luxation with an elevator is almost exclusively done with the elevator positioned from the buccal.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about extractions is FALSE?
options: Supporting the mandible during extraction of lower teeth is beneficial in reducing the chance of mandibular fracture and TMJ injury and increases patient comfort.
A bite block should be used to help support the mandible during extraction of lower teeth.
The surgeon’s non-dominant hand can be used for retraction during an extraction.
The surgeon’s non-dominant hand can be used to provide tactile feedback to the surgeon during an extraction.
None of these statements are FALSE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about cowhorn forceps is TRUE?
options: Cowhorn forceps generally will not be used for mandibular third molar extractions because these teeth often have conical fused roots without a distinct furcation.
Cowhorn forceps are an excellent choice for the extraction of any tooth with a distinct furcation.
Cowhorn forceps generally will not be used for mandibular third molar extractions because these teeth usually have three roots.
Cowhorn forceps are an excellent choice for maxillary third molar extractions.
A cowhorn forceps is also known as a universal forceps because they can be used for the extraction of any tooth.

questions.text: All of the following factors may increase the difficulty and/or risk involved in extracting primary teeth, EXCEPT:
options: The roots of primary teeth are often long and thin and can easily fracture.
The roots of primary teeth may resorb unevenly and if this occurs mid-root, there is an increased likelihood of fracture.
The roots of primary molars may converge and envelope the crown of the succedaneous tooth.  This may result in the succedaneous tooth being extracted with the primary tooth.
Delayed exfoliation of a primary tooth may result in the tooth being submerged relative to the adjacent teeth making access difficult.
A child may be anxious and uncooperative for dental procedures.
Proximity to the maxillary sinus or inferior alveolar nerve canal often increases the risk of significant permanent damage when primary teeth are extracted.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: Failure to remove excess granulation tissue surrounding a periodontally involved tooth at the time of extraction can result in increased bleeding.
Gauze pressure must be applied directly to an extraction site in order to be effective in achieving hemostasis.
Following extraction, the boney cortical plates should be compressed, provided this does not result in an alveolar ridge that becomes too narrow for implant placement.

If a fragment of buccal plate fractures during an extraction, the decision to remove or maintain the fragment will depend on both the size of the fragment and whether or not its soft tissue attachment can be maintained.
A throat screen only needs to be used at the final step of an extraction when the tooth is being delivered with the forceps.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE when planning a flap to extract a tooth?
options: An envelope flap should extend at least two teeth anterior to and one tooth posterior to the tooth being extracted.
An envelope flap should extend at least one tooth anterior to and two teeth posterior to the tooth being extracted.
A flap with an anterior vertical release should extend at least two teeth anterior to and one tooth posterior to the tooth being extracted.
A flap with both anterior and posterior vertical releases should extend at least two teeth anterior to and one tooth posterior to the tooth being extracted.
An envelope flap should extend at least two teeth anterior to and two teeth posterior to the tooth being extracted.

questions.text: You are extracting an impacted tooth from the palate. Consider the following statements: I. You should not incise the neurovascular bundle at the anterior palatine foramen because of the risk of severe uncontrollable bleeding. II. You should not incise the neurovascular bundle at the anterior palatine foramen because of the risk of a permanent significant neurosensory disturbance in the area. III. You should not make a releasing incision at the area of the greater palatine foramen because of the risk of causing difficult to control pulsatile bleeding. Which of the above statements is a TRUE statement that can help guide your surgical approach?
options: None of the statements (I, II, III) here are TRUE.

questions.text: Your patient presents with pain in their maxillary second bicuspid which has an active periapical infection.  The patient is not planning on replacing this tooth.  While you are extracting the tooth, it fractures. You take a radiograph and determine that the apical portion of the root, which measures approximately 2 mm, remains in it’s original position in the socket.  There is a periapical lesion present which indents the floor of the maxillary sinus. Consider the following statements: I. The fragment should be left in place since it is in its original position and is definitely less than 4 – 5 mm in length. II. The fragment should be left in place since it is deep in the alveolus. III. The fragment should be left in place since the patient is not planning on replacing the tooth with an implant. IV. If an attempt is made to remove the fragment, it may be displaced into the maxillary antrum. V. The fragment would be easier to remove if you had achieved good mobilization of the tooth prior to the occurrence of the fracture. Which of these statements is TRUE?
options: I, II, III, IV, and V.

questions.text: A new patient presents to your office for upper and lower full dentures. The patient has been edentulous for a long time and has a severely atrophic mandible.  The mandibular left bicuspid/molar area has several sharp boney projections that need to be smoothed out prior to denture construction.  Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: The mandible can be exposed with a crestal incision extending from the area of the canine to the area of the third molar without any risk of neurosensory disturbance..
The incision should be flared buccally in the third molar area to protect the mental nerve.
A series of short repeated scalpel strokes should be used to make the necessary incision.
It is not necessary to irrigate under the flap after the bone is smoothed with a bur and handpiece since the surgery was on bone only and there will not be any tooth debris under the flap.
None of these statements are TRUE.

questions.text: You are extracting a maxillary molar and decide that you need to section the tooth.  Consider the following statements: I. When sectioning the tooth, it is important to avoid drilling into the buccal and lingual cortical plates. II. When sectioning the tooth, it is important to avoid drilling into the interseptal bone. III. When sectioning the tooth, it is important to avoid drilling into the interradicular bone. Which of the above statements is a FALSE statement?
Which of the following statements about alveoplasty is FALSE?
options: Simple alveoplasty involves removal of bone.
Intraseptal alveoplasty involves removal of bone.
Simple alveoplasty involves exposure of the buccal cortical bone via elevation of a full-thickness mucoperiosteal flap which may result in post-operative bone resorption.
Intraseptal alveoplasty involves exposure of the buccal cortical bone via elevation of a full-thickness mucoperiosteal flap so that the ridge width can be narrowed without reducing height.
Simple alveoplasty is indicated when there are buccal bone irregularities while intraseptal alveoplasty is indicated when the buccal bone does not have irregularities.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about flaps for removal of maxillary and mandibular tori is FALSE?
options: Flap development may be difficult because the mucosa overlying the torus is often extremely thin.
Flap development may be difficult because the torus is often comprised of multiple lobes and the mucosa may extend into invaginations between the lobes or into peripheral undercuts.
Flap elevation may be made easier by injecting local anesthesia into the potential space between the bone and the periostium.
Since torus removal is strictly a boney procedure, soft tissue removal is not performed, even if excess tissue is present in the flapped tissue following bone reduction.
Wound dehiscence and flap necrosis are potential complications of torus removal.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the excision of hyperplastic tissue is TRUE?
options: After excision of a small area of hyperplastic tissue from the buccal surface of the alveolar ridge, primary closure can be performed, enabling healing by secondary intention.
After excision of a large area of hyperplastic tissue from the buccal surface of the alveolar ridge, the periosteum is removed and the wound left open, allowing healing by primary intention.
After excision of a large area of hyperplastic tissue from the buccal surface of the alveolar ridge, primary closure of the mucosal tissues may result in loss of vestibular depth.
A full-thickness mucoperiosteal flap should be elevated if the surgical plan involves suturing the mucosal margin to the periosteum.
When excising hyperplastic tissue, surgical technique is not important as each patient will heal differently depending on their medical history.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about frenectomies is FALSE?
options: A simple frenectomy involves excision of frenal tissue with suturing of mucosal margins to periostium at the depth of the vestibule.
A simple frenectomy may result in increased loss of vestibular depth when compared with a Z-plasty frenectomy

When treating a wide buccal frenum with a localized vestibuloplasty with secondary epithelialization, a supraperiosteal incision and dissection should be performed and the mucosal margin should be sutured to the periosteum at the maximum depth of the vestibule.
A stent or denture may be used following frenectomy procedures to help maintain vestibular depth.
When performing a lingual frenectomy, it is necessary to make the incision deep into the floor of the mouth to prevent regrowth of the frenum.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about a transpositional flap vestibuloplasty is FALSE?
options: This procedure is also referred to as a Lip Switch Procedure.
Adequate bone height of at least 15 mm is necessary for the procedure to be beneficial.
Adequate lingual vestibular depth is necessary for the procedure to be beneficial.

The procedure involves developing a thin labial mucosal flap which is extended into a supraperiosteal dissection on the anterior aspect of the mandible.  The flap is then sutured to the depth of the vestibule.
The procedure is very predictable and relapse is exceedingly rare.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about immediate dentures is TRUE?
options: Staging of extractions for immediate denture fabrication results in a better denture fit than if all anterior and posterior teeth were extracted at the time of denture insertion.
It is beneficial to extract posterior teeth first when fabricating immediate dentures as the patient can still smile with their remining anterior teeth.
After immediate dentures are inserted they should be left in for at least the first 24 - 48 hours, otherwise it may not be possible to immediately reinsert them due to swelling.
When planning immediate dentures, the patient should be informed that it is often necessary to make new dentures for a better fit after all healing has occurred.
All of these statements are TRUE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about diagnoses is TRUE?
options: A surgeon should always know the definitive diagnosis prior to performing any surgical procedure.
If a surgeon has no clue as to what a patient's diagnosis is, they should still perform a surgical procedure.
If a surgeon does not know the definitive diagnosis prior to performing a surgical procedure, they should develop a differential diagnosis including potential diagnoses.
The same treatment should always be performed for the same diagnosis.
A good surgeon can look at a pathologic lesion in a patient's mouth and know exactly what it is.

questions.text: All of the following are reasons that a dentist may obtain an inaccurate history, EXCEPT:
options: The patient has low health literacy.
The patient may be able to realize secondary gain by withholding or providing inaccurate information.
The patient is withholding information that they may be embarrassed by because they feel the dentist does not need to know that information.
The patient is a poor historian.
The patient and dentist are not fluent in the same language.
All of the above statements are reasons that a dentist may obtain an inaccurate history.

questions.text: Consider the following two patients. F. 56 year-old female who had a hysterectomy 2 years ago and is hypothyroid following thyroidectomy for thyroid cancer. M. 56 year-old male who ran marathons up until 8 months ago when he had 2 stents placed when he had a heart attack. What ASA classification would you assign to each patient:
options: F = ASA II and M = ASA III.
F = ASA III and M = ASA IV.
F = ASA III and M = ASA III.
F = ASA IV and M = ASA IV.
F = ASA III and M = ASA II.
F = ASA II and M = ASA IV.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about disturbances in hemostasis is FALSE?
options: If a patient has a significant bleeding episode following a surgical procedure, the surgeon did not necessarily make an error in judgement or technique.
NSAIDS may cause coagulation problems following a surgical procedure but acetaminophen will not.
Once a patient has been diagnosed with a hemophilia or quantitative platelet disorder, their bleeding risk remains constant, unless some corrective treatment is provided.
DDAVP and corticosteroids can both be effective in elevating blood levels of a patient's coagulation factors and platelets.

Medical personnel should always be suspicious that patients with prosthetic heart valves, atrial fibrillation, DVT's (deep vein thromboses), and PE's (pulmonary emboli), and patients following coronary artery stenting are anti-coagulated and thus have an increased bleeding risk.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: A patient on a target specific anticoagulant should have blood tests prior to a planned extraction to check if their INR is 2.5 or below and the extraction can be done.
A patient on a target specific anticoagulant should have blood tests prior to a planned extraction to check if their INR is 4.0 or below and the extraction can be done.

Although INR monitoring is mandatory for patients on target specific anticoagulants so that their medication dose can be adjusted as needed, this monitoring is often done at less frequent intervals than for patients on warfarin.
The target INR for all patients is the same, even if they are being anticoagulated for different conditions.
NONE of these statements is TRUE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about “bridging” is TRUE?
options: This technique is useful for minimizing the risk to a patient on warfarin if their anticoagulation needs to be interrupted for a procedure.
This technique involves stopping the patient's anticoagulation for 10 days both before and after the procedure.
This technique is useful for patients with a low clotting risk who will be undergoing a low bleeding risk procedure.
During bridging, a patient should never be on two anticoagulants at the same time.
An advantage of this technique is that no blood tests need to be performed.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about vaso-vagal syncope is FALSE?
options: Dental providers should be knowledgeable about the prevention of vaso-vagal syncope as this occurrence makes up approximately 50% of all medical emergencies that occur in the dental office.
When vaso-vagal syncope occurs, blood pressure decreases and heart rate increases.
Pre-operative hydration can be helpful in preventing vaso-vagal syncope.
Supplemental oxygen delivery can be helpful in preventing vaso-vagal syncope.
Physiological and psychologic factors can both contribute to the occurrence of vaso-vagal syncope.

questions.text: Which of the following conditions does NOT put patients at increased risk of infection?
Which of the following statements about diabetic patients is FALSE?
options: Compared to non-diabetic patients, both well-controlled and poorly-controlled diabetics have an increased risk of infection.
Compared to non-diabetic patients, infections are more difficult to control in both well-controlled and poorly-controlled diabetics.
Insulin doses should be adjusted based on pre-op intake for diabetics undergoing oral surgical procedures.
Insulin doses should be adjusted based on anticipated post-op intake for diabetics undergoing oral surgical procedures.
Mild-moderate hyperglycemia is preferred over hypoglycemia in diabetics in the peri-operative period.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about antibiotic prophylaxis is FALSE?
options: Bacteremia resulting from surgical manipulation during oral surgery can cause bacterial seeding of a damaged native or prosthetic valve resulting in subacute bacterial endocarditis.
If a patient already on antibiotics requires antibiotic prophylaxis prior to an oral surgical procedure, an antibiotic from another class should be used to reduce the risk from resistant organisms.
Prophylactic antibiotics are generally not recommended prior to oral surgical treatment to prevent prosthetic joint infection.
Patients with immunocompromising medical conditions or joint replacement complications may require prophylactic antibiotics prior to oral surgical treatment to prevent prosthetic joint infection.
None of these statements is FALSE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about adrenally suppressed patients is FALSE?
options: Complex prolonged surgery may cause adrenal crisis in adrenally suppressed patients.
Adrenally suppressed patients undergoing most dental procedures do not require supplemental steroids.

If a surgical procedure requires steroid supplementation for a patient on steroids at the time of surgery, additional doses of steroids should be given on the day before surgery, the day of surgery, and the day following surgery.

If a patient was on 10 mg or more of hydrocortisone for 1 week or more within the previous year and they are undergoing a procedure that would require steroid supplementation, steroids should be given in increasing doses for 2 weeks beginning the day before the surgery.
If adrenal crisis develops in an adrenally suppressed patient, symptoms may include hypotension, increased pulse, syncope, nausea, and fever.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a sign of a cerebrovascular accident?
options: Loss of balance, headache, or dizziness.
One side of the face is drooping.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about treating infected teeth is FALSE?
options: If a dentoalveolar abscess arises from pulpal involvement of a tooth, the surgeon must wait for complete resolution of the infection prior to extracting the tooth.
The most rapid resolution of an acute dentoalveolar infection caused by pulpal involvement of a tooth will be achieved by extraction of that tooth.
Trismus from an infected tooth may complicate extraction of the tooth.
Tooth related infection may make it more difficult to achieve adequate local anesthesia for extraction.
Extraction of an impacted third molar in the presence of severe pericoronitis is accompanied by an increased incidence of complications.

questions.text: Consider the following radiographs showing primary teeth requiring extraction. Which accompanying statement is FALSE?
options: The mandibular left primary second molar seen in this radiograph may be difficult to extract because it is submerged and potentially ankylosed.

The mandibular right primary second molar seen in this periapical radiograph may be difficult to extract because it has been root canal treated, has a large restoration, and has not had any resorption of its roots.
The mandibular left primary first and second molars seen in this periapical radiograph should be easy to extract because the roots appear to be significantly resorbed.
The mandibular right primary second molar seen in this periapical radiograph may be difficult to extract because the mesial root is thin and has not had any resorption of its length.

The mandibular right primary second molar seen in this periapical radiograph may be difficult to extract because it has widespread roots and if extraction necessitates sectioning of the tooth, the succedaneous premolar tooth bud is at risk of being damaged.

questions.text: Consider the periapical radiographs below and the statements that follow: EXTERNAL RESORPTION INTERNAL RESORPTION Statement I: Extraction of the tooth undergoing external resorption may be difficult as the tooth may be prone to fracture. Statement II: Extraction of the tooth undergoing internal resorption may be difficult as the tooth may be prone to fracture. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?
options: I and II are both TRUE.
I and II are both FALSE.

questions.text: You are extracting a mandibular second premolar. You have achieved adequate mobility of the tooth with a straight elevator. You are now using a 151 forceps but cannot complete the extraction because the beaks keep sliding around on the tooth. Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: You are using a forceps designed for maxillary teeth and should switch to a 150 forceps which, unlike the 151 forceps, is designed for extracting mandibular teeth.
An Ash forceps may be more effective as the beaks may grasp the tooth more effectively.
Adjusting the beaks of the forceps so that they are seated as apically as possible may be helpful.
Adjusting the beaks of the forceps so that they are better seated along the long axis of the tooth may be helpful.
All of these strategies may be helpful.

questions.text: Consider the following statements: I. Tooth and/or bone fragments or debris left at the surgical site may result in post-operative infection. II. Surgical handpieces blow air into the surgical field to clear the field of tooth and/ or bone fragments and debris that result from drilling into teeth or bone. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?
options: I and II are both TRUE.
I and II are both FALSE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements describing the use of a scalpel to make an incision is FALSE?
options: When making an incision with a scalpel, mobile tissues should be stabilized.
The mucosa, submucosal tissues, and periosteum should each be incised in a separate cutting motion.
A “pen grasp” should be used to maintain maximum control.
A “15 blade” is most commonly used for oral surgical procedures.
None of these statements are FALSE.

questions.text: Which of the following instruments CANNOT be used for bone removal?
options: All of these instruments can be used for bone removal.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the use of straight elevators is TRUE?
options: Forceful movements are required to achieve adequate mobility of a tooth.
The convex surface of the elevator should be applied to the tooth being extracted.
They can only be used when adjacent teeth are present to manipulate against.
A “pen grasp” should be used to apply maximum force.
None of these statements is TRUE.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the use of periotomes for extractions is FALSE?
options: They may be advantageous for preserving socket anatomy when performing extractions.
They are used to sever PDL fibers.
They are only used effectively in the first 2 - 3 mm of the PDL space.
They are used by applying apically directed pressure circumferentially around the tooth
Eventual delivery of the tooth is accomplished with forceps.

questions.text: “Surgical” or “open” extraction technique is indicated for all of the following EXCEPT:
options: When excess force would otherwise be necessary.
When a substantial portion of the crown is missing or covered by tissue.
When access to the root or fragment of the root is difficult or limited.
When closed technique would pose additional risk to vital structures.
When the tooth to be extracted has advanced periodontal disease.

questions.text: All of the following are useful techniques for performing extractions, EXCEPT:
options: When extracting mandibular teeth, the jaw should be supported by having the patient bite on a bite block.
When extracting maxillary teeth, the jaw should be supported by the operator or assistant pushing up on the patient's chin.
The operator's non-dominant hand and/or fingers can be useful for retracting.
The operator's non-dominant hand and/or fingers can be useful for tactile purposes such as determining if inadvertent mobilization of an adjacent tooth or restoration is occurring.
The operator's non-dominant hand and/or fingers can be useful for controlling tooth/restoration fragments that may fracture off during an extraction.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the effects of tooth-specific factors on difficulty of extraction is FALSE?
options: Extraction of maxillary lateral incisors may be complicated by distal curvature of the root.
Maxillary second premolars and single rooted first premolars generally have conical roots, making them amenable to extraction by rotational movements.

Extraction of maxillary second molars is generally easier than extraction of maxillary first molars because their roots are generally shorter and less divergent, and their buccal roots are often fused.
Although mandibular premolars often have conical roots making them amenable to extraction by rotation, extraction may be made more difficult due to roots that are curved or have bulbous apices.
Extraction of mandibular second molars may be more difficult than extraction of mandibular first molars because they generally have roots that are more widely divergent.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about extractions is FALSE?
options: The treatment plan for subsequent tooth replacement should be considered when determining the extraction technique to be used.
Surgical extraction techniques generally provide greater access to safely remove a tooth or root.
Surgical extraction techniques do not allow for contouring or smoothing of bone at the time of extraction.
Compared to surgical extraction techniques, closed extraction techniques may be more traumatic or morbid, resulting in a greater likelihood of unintended crown or root fracture.
Compared to surgical extraction techniques, closed extraction techniques may be more traumatic or morbid, with an increased risk of sinus exposure when extracting maxillary posterior teeth.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding surgical flaps is FALSE?
options: When designing a flap, the base should be broader than free margin, allowing for an adequate blood supply to prevent ischemic necrosis of the flap.
Periosteum should be preserved as it is the primary tissue responsible for bone healing.
Improper placement of an incision can result in wound dehiscence and delayed healing.
Incisions in the retromolar region of the mandible should be flared to the buccal to minimize the risk of damaging the lingual nerve.
Releasing incisions carry a much higher risk of complications at the anterior palatine foramen region when compared to the greater palatine foramen region.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about elevating a flap is FALSE?
options: A sharp scalpel blade should be used when making an incision.
The spearpoint end of the periosteal elevator should be used to elevate the flap.
When elevating a flap, it is most effective and least damaging to the papilla to elevate from the angled length of the papilla rather than from the apex of the papilla.
Injecting local anesthesia under the periosteum will make it more difficult to elevate a full thickness mucoperiosteal flap.
A retractor should be positioned to rest on bone without placing tension on the soft tissues.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about surgical extractions is TRUE?
options: The beaks of an extraction forceps should never be placed on the bone overlying a root to be extracted.

If limited access is preventing extraction of a fractured root, elevation of a flap may enable extraction by allowing for adequate positioning of an elevator and/or forceps, even without removing bone.
Once an extraction is begun, all root fragments should be removed, no matter how much bone needs to be removed to accomplish their removal.
After completing an open extraction, the operator should directly palpate the exposed bony edges and aggressively smooth any sharp areas.

Irrigation prior to closing a flap is only necessary if there may be tooth fragments or debris under the flap as they may result in post-operative infection. Bone fragments or debris cannot result in post-operative infection.

questions.text: Consider the following statements about bone removal during surgical extractions: I. When sectioning a multi-rooted tooth for extraction, it is important to preserve the buccal and lingual/palatal cortical plates. II. When sectioning a multi-rooted tooth for extraction, it is important to preserve the interseptal bone - the bone between the tooth being extracted and the adjacent teeth). III. When sectioning a multi-rooted tooth for extraction, it is important to preserve the interradicular bone - the bone between the individual roots of the tooth being extracted. Which of the following is correct:
options: Only I and II are TRUE.
Only I and III are TRUE.
Only II and III are TRUE.
I, II, and III are TRUE.

questions.text: Hard and soft tissue surgical procedures are often necessary prior to designing and fabricating prostheses for patients. All of the following are necessary when evaluating a patient for a prosthesis EXCEPT:
options: Radiograph examination for the presence of impacted teeth, retained roots, and pathology.
Radiograph examination for the location of the mental and lingual nerves.
Visual examination and palpation for bony undercuts, protuberances, tori, exostoses, post-tuberosity notching, height of palatal vault, and depth of vestibules.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about INTRASEPTAL ALVEOPLASTY is FALSE?
options: This procedure is indicated when contouring of irregularities of the buccal bone is necessary.
This procedure results in decreased alveolar ridge thickness.
This procedure maintains alveolar ridge height.
This procedure is useful for the reduction or elimination of buccal undercuts.
This procedure involves the use of a rongeur and/or a surgical handpiece and bur for cutting intraseptal bone.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about pre-prosthetic surgery is FALSE?
options: Maxillary torus reduction may be made more difficult because the overlying mucosa may be thin and extend into the invaginations between the lobes of the torus.
Mandibular torus reduction may be made more difficult because the overlying mucosa may be thin and extend into the invaginations between the lobes of the torus.
In some cases maxillary or mandibular torus reduction may be effectively accomplished by reduction of excess soft tissue only.
Infection may result from displacement of bone fragments or debris into the floor of the mouth during mandibular torus reduction.
Oro-nasal communication may result as a complication of maxillary tuberosity reduction.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: When performing soft tissue pre-prosthetic procedures, the operator must be aware that their choice of technique may cause a reduction in vestibular depth.
When performing pre-prosthetic procedures, the operator must be aware that the location where the inferior alveolar nerve exits the mandible may have been altered due to resorption of the mandible.

When performing soft tissue pre-prosthetic procedures, the operator should use a technique that achieves healing by primary intention to achieve the optimal result while promoting the quickest healing and most comfortable post-operative recovery.

When incising the frenum along the base of the tongue during a lingual frenectomy, the operator should cut along a clamp as this helps to avoid cutting into the floor of the mouth and aids in hemostasis.
When removing an epulis, the operator may use different techniques based on the amount of tissue that needs to be removed.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the transpositional flap vestibuloplasty is TRUE?
options: All incisions should be made to develop full thickness mucoperiosteal flaps.
The height of the bone does not matter as this is a soft tissue procedure intended to increase the facial vestibular depth.
The lingual vestibular depth does not matter as this procedure is intended to increase the facial vestibular depth.
This procedure yields reliable predictable results.
This procedure does not involve placement of a skin graft.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the submucosal vestibuloplasty for maxillary ridge extension is FALSE?
options: This procedure is used to achieve better stability and retention of maxillary dentures.
Adequate pre-operative evaluation must be performed to avoid esthetic changes such as shortening or inversion of the upper lip.
A splint is used to hold the mucosa against the periosteum at the depth of vestibule until healing has occurred.
Submucosal and supraperiosteal tunneling is performed so that tissues can be effectively repositioned without the actual excision of any tissue.
An anterior vertical incision is used to allow entry for submucosal and supraperiosteal tunneling.

questions.text: BONUS: A throat screen should be used to minimize the risk of aspiration or ingestion of objects such as teeth, restorations, small instruments and other objects.
Which of the following statements regarding tooth extractions is FALSE?
options: When extracting a tooth, it is important to know what the subsequent restorative treatment plan is.
An open or surgical extraction technique may prevent an oro-antral communication during an extraction procedure.
An open or surgical extraction technique enables bone recontouring during an extraction procedure.
An open or surgical extraction technique increases the likelihood of alveolar bone loss or sinus exposure during an extraction procedure when compared to a closed extraction technique.
A closed extraction technique does not require the development of a flap.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding incisions and flap development is FALSE?
options: There will be less bleeding with a FTMPF than a split thickness flap because the tissue plane between bone and periosteum is relatively avascular.

When developing a flap in the mandibular bicuspid region of an atrophic mandible, a crestal incision should be utilized instead of an incision with vertical releases to ensure that the mental nerve will not be damaged.
An incision should be placed at least 6 - 8 mm away from a cortical bone defect to prevent the tissue from collapsing into the bony defect and resulting in wound dehiscence.
Incision at the anterior palatine foramen carries less risk of bleeding and nerve damage than incision at the greater palatine foramen.
A vertical releasing incision should cross the free gingival margin at the line angle of a tooth and should not be made over a bony prominence.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding a semi-lunar flap is FALSE?
options: It provides good access to the apices of teeth in the surgical field.
It enables the surgeon to avoid causing trauma to the papillae and gingival margin of the flap.
Overall surgical access may be limited because visibility of the entire root area is not provided.
It is useful for periapical surgery.
The incision to create a semi-lunar flap can only cross a periodontal pocket if the pocket is 3 mm or less in depth.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding bone removal during tooth extraction is FALSE?
options: Bone removal during extraction allows for increased visualization of the tooth being extracted.
Bone removal during extraction may be performed to lessen or eliminate an impedance in the path of removal of that tooth.
When bone is removed during tooth extraction, it is more important to preserve the buccal and lingual cortical plates and intraseptal bone than the interradicular bone.
When using a drill to remove bone during a tooth extraction, a surgical handpiece which exhausts air out the rear of the handpiece should be used
When sectioning a multi-rooted tooth during extraction, it is necessary to first remove bone.

questions.text: You are extracting all of a patient's remaining teeth, specifically teeth 6, 7, 8. 9, 10, 11, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, and 27. Which of the following statements regarding these extractions is TRUE?
options: When extracting the maxillary teeth, 6 and 11 should be extracted first.
When extracting the maxillary teeth, 6 and 11 should be extracted last.
When extracting the maxillary teeth, the sequencing of extracting 6 and 11 may vary depending on the specific circumstances which are present.
When extracting all of these teeth, it is important to apply all concepts involved in extracting teeth, including being careful to not luxate an adjacent tooth when using an elevator.
It is necessary to extract the mandibular teeth before extracting the maxillary teeth.

questions.text: A maxillary tuberosity requires reduction because of vertical and horizontal boney excess. Which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: Since the procedure is being performed because of excess bone, there is no reason to excise any soft tissue.
Since bone will be removed, a full thickness mucoperiosteal flap will need to be elevated to achieve the necessary access.
Bone can be removed with a bone file, a rongeur, and/or a handpiece and bur.
It is important to utilize appropriate imaging to ensure that bone removal will not violate the maxillary sinus.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding changes associated with tooth loss and bone atrophy is FALSE?
options: After teeth are lost, the maxillary crest shifts palatally &medially.
After teeth are lost, upper lip support diminishes resulting in a “sunken face” look.
After teeth are lost, the mandibular crest shifts inferiorly and laterally.
After teeth are lost, resorption of the maxilla and mandible results in a Class III or prognathic appearance.
The rate of bone resorption increases as more time passes after an extraction.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding alveoplasty is TRUE?
options: Simple alveoplasty requires a full thickness mucoperiosteal flap.
Intraseptal alveoplasty requires a full thickness mucoperiosteal flap.
Intraseptal alveoplasty is useful for recontouring buccal irregularities.
Intraseptal alveoplasty can be utilized to increase ridge width.
A disadvantage of intraseptal alveoplasty is the resultant loss of ridge height.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding soft tissue preprosthetic surgery procedures is TRUE?
